title: Process: The diagram below shows two different processes for manufacturing black tea. Sum...
description: The diagram below shows two different processes for manufacturing black tea. Summarize the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.
guide_html:
HƯỚNG DẪN VIẾT BÀI

Two different processes for manufacturing black tea

1. Giải thích đề

Sơ đồ mô tả hai quy trình khác nhau để sản xuất trà đen:

  • phương pháp truyền thống (loose tea)
  • phương pháp hiện đại (tea bags)

→ Dạng: process \+ comparison

2. Introduction (paraphrase)

Giữ:

  • manufacturing black tea

Dùng:

  • shows → illustrates / compares
  • different → two distinct

Ví dụ:

The diagram illustrates two different processes for manufacturing black tea using traditional and modern methods.

3. Overview (ý chính)

  • Cả hai quy trình đều bắt đầu bằng:

→ picking \+ withering

  • Sau đó chia thành 2 hướng:

→ rolling (traditional)

→ cutting (modern)

  • Cuối cùng:

→ đều trải qua oxidation \+ drying

→ Key idea:

  • Khác nhau ở giai đoạn xử lý lá trà
  • Nhưng giống nhau ở các bước cuối

4. Chia BODY

BODY 1 – Giai đoạn chung (initial stages)

  • Đầu tiên:

→ lá trà tươi được hái (picking)

→ chỉ lấy buds và top leaves

  • Sau đó:

→ withering (làm héo)

→ không khí được thổi qua lá

→ khoảng 60% độ ẩm bị loại bỏ

BODY 2 – Hai phương pháp khác nhau

Traditional method (loose tea):

  • Lá được rolling (cán/vo)
  • Lá bị dập và giải phóng enzyme

Modern method (tea bags):

  • Lá được cut, torn and curled (CTC)
  • Tạo ra hạt nhỏ hơn
  • Quy trình nhanh hơn

→ Ý so sánh:

  • Traditional \= giữ dạng lá
  • Modern \= nhỏ, nhanh, công nghiệp hơn

BODY 3 – Giai đoạn cuối (giống nhau)

  • Cả hai:

→ trải qua oxidation/fermentation

→ enzyme \+ không khí → lá chuyển màu đồng (copper)

  • Sau đó:

→ firing/drying trong lò hoặc máy sấy

  • Kết quả:

→ hương vị và mùi thơm được tạo ra

→ tổng cộng 97% độ ẩm bị loại bỏ

5. Gợi ý từ vựng

  • be picked → được hái
  • be withered → được làm héo
  • moisture → độ ẩm
  • be rolled / crushed → được cán / nghiền
  • release enzymes → giải phóng enzyme
  • undergo oxidation → trải qua quá trình oxy hóa
  • turn copper colour → chuyển màu đồng
  • be dried → được sấy khô
  • final product → sản phẩm cuối

The diagram illustrates two different processes used to manufacture black tea: a traditional method for loose tea and a modern method for tea bags.

Overall, both processes begin with the picking of fresh tea leaves and a withering stage, after which they diverge into separate techniques before converging again for oxidation and final drying.

Initially, only the buds and top leaves are selected and then left to wither, during which air is passed through them to remove around 60% of their moisture content. Following this, the process splits. In the traditional method, the leaves are rolled flat and broken, which releases enzymes. By contrast, in the modern method, the leaves are cut, torn and curled into smaller granules, allowing for a quicker processing time.

After these stages, both types of leaves undergo oxidation or fermentation. During this phase, the leaves are spread out and exposed to air, causing a chemical reaction that turns them a copper colour. Finally, the leaves are fired or dried using ovens or hot air dryers, which removes up to 97% of the remaining moisture and enhances the tea’s flavour and aroma.
chart_description:
TYPE: process diagram
TITLE: Two different processes for manufacturing black tea
UNITS/AXES: Not applicable
SERIES/CATEGORIES: Not applicable
DATA:
Stage 1: Picking fresh tea leaves. Input: Only buds & top leaves picked for good quality tea.
Stage 2: Withering. Input: air passed through leaves on rack. Output: 60% moisture out.
Stage 3a (Traditional method - Loose tea): ROLLING. Input: leaves rolled flat and broken. Output: enzymes released from leaves.
Stage 3b (Modern method - Tea bags): CUTTING. Input: leaves cut, torn and curled. Output: quick process/smaller granular pieces created.
Stage 4: Oxidation/Fermentation. Input: rolled leaves spread on tiles/cement, enzymes + air. Output: leaves change to copper colour.
Stage 5: Firing/Drying. Input: in oven/hot air dryers. Output: flavour and aroma released, 97% moisture out (in total).
KEY FEATURES:
* The process begins with picking fresh tea leaves, specifically buds and top leaves.
* The initial step for both methods is withering, which removes 60% of the moisture.
* After withering, the process splits into two distinct methods: traditional (loose tea) involving rolling, and modern (tea bags) involving cutting.
* Both methods lead to an oxidation/fermentation stage where leaves change to a copper colour due to enzymes and air.
* The final stage for both methods is firing/drying, which releases flavour and aroma and removes a total of 97% moisture.

title: Process: The diagram below shows how honey is made in small-scale commercial production. ...
description: The diagram below shows how honey is made in small-scale commercial production. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.
guide_html:
HƯỚNG DẪN VIẾT BÀI

Small-scale commercial honey production

1. Giải thích đề

Sơ đồ cho thấy quy trình sản xuất mật ong quy mô nhỏ, bao gồm hai giai đoạn: quá trình tự nhiên của ong và quá trình xử lý của con người.

→ Dạng: process (2 stages: natural \+ man-made)

2. Introduction (paraphrase)

Giữ:

  • honey production – bees – humans

Dùng:

  • shows → illustrates / outlines
  • process → procedure

Ví dụ:

The diagram illustrates the process of small-scale commercial honey production, including both the bee phase and the human processing stage.

3. Overview (ý chính)

  • Quy trình gồm 2 giai đoạn chính:

1. Ong tạo mật trong tổ

2. Con người thu hoạch và xử lý mật

  • Đặc điểm:

→ từ nectar → honey → refined product → sold

4. Chia BODY

BODY 1 – Bee phase

  • Đầu tiên:

→ ong thu thập mật hoa (nectar) từ hoa

  • Sau đó:

→ nectar được đưa về tổ và lưu trữ trong các ô tổ ong

  • Tiếp theo:

→ ong quạt cánh để làm khô (drying) mật

  • Cuối cùng:

→ các ô được làm sạch và niêm phong bằng sáp (wax)

→ Kết quả: hình thành mật ong hoàn chỉnh trong tổ

BODY 2 – Human phase

  • Bước đầu:

→ con người thu thập honeycombs

  • Sau đó:

→ tổ ong được ép (pressing) để lấy mật

  • Tiếp theo:

→ mật được đun nóng ở 45–50°C

  • Rồi:

→ được lọc qua sieve tank để loại bỏ tạp chất

  • Sau đó:

→ được để lắng trong 2–4 ngày (settling tank)

  • Cuối cùng:

→ mật được đóng chai và bán ra thị trường

5. Gợi ý từ vựng

  • nectar → mật hoa
  • honeycomb → tổ ong
  • be deposited → được đưa vào
  • be dried → được làm khô
  • be sealed → được niêm phong
  • be extracted → được chiết xuất
  • be filtered → được lọc
  • impurities → tạp chất
  • final product → sản phẩm cuối cùng

The diagram illustrates the process of small-scale commercial honey production, which involves both natural activities carried out by bees and subsequent human processing stages.

Overall, the production consists of two main phases: the bee phase, where nectar is transformed into honey and stored in honeycombs, and the human phase, where the honey is extracted, processed, and prepared for sale.

In the first phase, bees begin by gathering nectar from flowers. This nectar is then deposited into honeycomb cells inside the hive. After that, bees dry the liquid by fanning it with their wings, reducing its moisture content. Finally, the cells are cleaned and sealed with wax, indicating that the honey is ready for collection.

In the second phase, humans harvest the honeycombs from the hive. These combs are then pressed to extract the raw honey. The extracted liquid is heated at a temperature of around 45–50°C before being passed through a sieve tank to remove impurities such as dirt or wax. Next, the honey is transferred to a settling tank, where it is left for 2–4 days. In the final step, the purified honey is packaged into jars and distributed for sale.
chart_description:
TYPE: process diagram
TITLE: Small-scale commercial honey production
UNITS/AXES: Temperature in degrees Celsius (°C), time in days
SERIES/CATEGORIES: Not applicable
DATA:
**BEE PHASE**
1. Gathering nectar: A bee is shown on a pink flower.
2. Depositing honey: A bee hive is shown.
3. Drying honey: Two bees are on a honeycomb with honey dripping. Text labels "Fan wings" point to the wings of the larger bee.
4. Keeping cells clean: Two bees are on a honeycomb. Text labels "Keeping cells clean" and "Seal cells (with wax)" with an arrow pointing to the sealed cells.

**HUMAN PHASE**
A. Gathering honeycombs: A person in a beekeeper suit is gathering honeycombs from a beehive.
B. Pressing combs: A person is pressing honeycombs into a wooden container, producing "Honey".
C. Heating 45-50°C: A person is pouring honey from a black container into a wooden container, which is labelled "Heating 45-50°C".
D. Sieve tank (removing dirt etc): Honey flows from the heating tank into a sieve tank.
E. Settling tank (for 2-4 days): Honey flows from the sieve tank into a settling tank.
F. Selling honey: Honey from the settling tank is put into jars, which are then loaded into a red van labelled "HONEY" for selling.

KEY FEATURES:
* The process is divided into two main phases: the Bee Phase and the Human Phase.
* The Bee Phase involves four steps: gathering nectar, depositing honey, drying honey, and keeping cells clean.
* The Human Phase begins with gathering honeycombs and ends with selling honey.
* Key steps in the human processing include pressing combs, heating, sieving, and settling.
* The honey is heated to 45-50°C and settled for 2-4 days before packaging.

title: Process: The diagram details the process of producing olive oil. Summarise the informatio...
description: The diagram details the process of producing olive oil. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.
guide_html:
HƯỚNG DẪN VIẾT BÀI

Olive oil production process

1. Giải thích đề

Sơ đồ mô tả quy trình sản xuất dầu ô liu từ lúc thu hoạch đến khi lưu trữ.

→ Dạng: process (quy trình nhiều bước, có phụ phẩm)

2. Introduction (paraphrase)

Giữ:

  • olive oil – production

Dùng:

  • shows → illustrates / outlines
  • process → procedure

Ví dụ:

The diagram illustrates the process of producing olive oil.

3. Overview (ý chính)

  • Quy trình gồm nhiều giai đoạn:

harvesting → cleaning → crushing → extracting → separating → storage

  • Ô liu được chuyển thành olive paste, sau đó ép để lấy dầu
  • Sản phẩm cuối là virgin oil, trong khi phần còn lại tạo ra waste water và pomace

→ Có cả sản phẩm chính và phụ phẩm

4. Chia BODY

BODY 1 – Giai đoạn đầu (thu hoạch → tạo paste)

  • Ô liu được thu hoạch (harvesting)
  • Sau đó:
  • đưa vào collection vat
  • Tiếp theo:
  • de-leafing và washing để loại bỏ lá và bụi bẩn
  • Ô liu sạch được:
  • đưa vào crusher
  • tạo thành olive paste
  • Hỗn hợp này tiếp tục được xử lý trong:
  • malaxer (dưới 27°C)

→ Ý: xử lý cơ học để chuẩn bị chiết xuất

BODY 2 – Giai đoạn sau (tách dầu → lưu trữ)

  • Hỗn hợp được đưa vào:
  • centrifugal press

→ tại đây:

  • tách thành:
  • pomace (bã)
  • và chất lỏng chứa dầu
  • Chất lỏng tiếp tục:
  • qua decantation để tách solids & water
  • Sau đó:
  • qua separation để loại bỏ waste water
  • Cuối cùng:
  • dầu tinh khiết (virgin oil) được đưa vào storage tank

→ Ý: tách dần → tinh lọc → lưu trữ

5. Gợi ý từ vựng

  • be harvested → được thu hoạch
  • be washed → được rửa sạch
  • be crushed → được nghiền
  • be processed into → được chuyển thành
  • be extracted → được chiết xuất
  • be separated from → được tách khỏi
  • by-product → sản phẩm phụ

The diagram illustrates the process of producing olive oil from fresh olives.

Overall, the process involves several stages, beginning with harvesting and ending with storage, while waste materials are removed at different points.

Initially, olives are picked from trees and collected in a vat. They are then washed and de-leafed to remove impurities before being crushed in a mill to form olive paste. This paste is transferred to a malaxer, where it is slowly mixed at a controlled temperature of below 27°C.

Next, the mixture is processed in a centrifugal press, which separates the paste into different components. Solid waste, known as pomace, is removed and can be further processed elsewhere. The remaining liquid undergoes decantation to separate oil from water and solids.

Finally, the oil is further purified through a separation stage, where waste water is removed. The finished virgin oil is then stored in a storage tank for later use.
chart_description:
TYPE: process diagram
TITLE: none
UNITS/AXES: Temperature in Malaxer (<27°C)
SERIES/CATEGORIES: Harvesting, Collection vat, De-leafing washing, Olive mill, Crushing, Olive paste, Malaxer, Centrifugal press, Pomace, Virgin oils, Seperation, Waste water, Decantation, Solids & water, Storage tank
DATA:
1. Harvesting: Olives are harvested from trees.
2. Collection vat: Harvested olives are placed in a collection vat.
3. De-leafing washing: Olives from the collection vat undergo de-leafing and washing.
4. Olive mill (Crushing): Washed olives are sent to an olive mill for crushing.
5. Olive paste: The output of the olive mill is olive paste.
6. Malaxer (<27°C): Olive paste is transferred to a malaxer, where it is processed at a temperature below 27°C.
7. Centrifugal press: The output from the malaxer goes into a centrifugal press.
8. Pomace: One output from the centrifugal press is pomace, which can be processed further at refining factories.
9. Virgin oils: Another output from the centrifugal press is virgin oils.
10. Seperation: Virgin oils undergo separation, producing waste water as a byproduct.
11. Decantation: Virgin oils also undergo decantation, producing solids & water as a byproduct.
12. Storage tank: The final product, after separation and decantation, is stored in a storage tank.
KEY FEATURES:
* The process begins with harvesting olives from trees.
* Olives are washed and then crushed to form olive paste.
* The olive paste is malaxed at a controlled temperature before being pressed.
* A centrifugal press separates the olive paste into virgin oils and pomace.
* Virgin oils undergo further purification through separation and decantation.

title: Process: The diagram shows a process of making a storage area from a material called conc...
description: The diagram shows a process of making a storage area from a material called concrete canvas. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and making comparisons where relevant.
guide_html:
HƯỚNG DẪN VIẾT BÀI

1. Giải thích đề

Sơ đồ mô tả quy trình tạo ra một khu lưu trữ bằng vật liệu gọi là concrete canvas.

→ Dạng: process (man-made, linear, nhiều bước)

2. Introduction (paraphrase)

The diagram illustrates the process of creating a storage area using concrete canvas.

3. Overview (ý chính)

  • Quy trình gồm 8 bước chính, từ sản xuất đến sử dụng
  • Có thể chia thành 3 giai đoạn:

→ manufacturing & delivery → installation → hardening & usage

  • Điểm nổi bật:

→ vật liệu ban đầu mềm (dạng cuộn) nhưng trở nên cứng sau khi được làm ướt

4. Body chia logic

BODY 1 – Manufacturing → Delivery → Preparation

  • Ban đầu:

→ concrete canvas được sản xuất với 3 lớp:

  • fibrous surface
  • dry concrete
  • waterproof layer
  • Sau đó:

→ vật liệu được cuộn lại và vận chuyển bằng xe tải

  • Khi đến nơi:

→ được unwrapped (mở ra)

BODY 2 – Installation \+ shaping

  • Tiếp theo:

→ tấm canvas được trải trên mặt đất

  • Sau đó:

→ được cố định bằng pegs

  • Một máy bơm:

→ pumps air into the structure

→ Kết quả:

  • tạo thành hình mái vòm (arched structure)

BODY 3 – Hardening \+ final use

  • Tiếp theo:

→ nước được phun lên bề mặt (hydrating)

  • Sau khoảng:

→ 20–24 hours, vật liệu sets and hardens

  • Cuối cùng:

→ cấu trúc được sử dụng như a storage area

5. Từ vựng ăn điểm

  • concrete canvas → vải bê tông
  • fibrous surface → bề mặt sợi
  • waterproof layer → lớp chống nước
  • unwrap → tháo cuộn
  • spread on the ground → trải trên mặt đất
  • peg → cọc cố định
  • pump air → bơm khí
  • hydrate → làm ướt
  • set / harden → đông cứng
  • storage facility → khu lưu trữ

The diagram illustrates how a storage area is constructed using concrete canvas.

Overall, the process involves eight main stages, beginning with the manufacture of the canvas and ending with a fully formed storage structure. Key steps include delivering and preparing the material, inflating it with air, hydrating it, and allowing it to harden.

Initially, the concrete canvas is produced with three layers: a fibrous top surface, a dry concrete layer, and a waterproof backing. The material is then rolled up and delivered to the construction site. After delivery, it is unwrapped and the protective cover is removed.

Next, the canvas is spread flat on the ground and secured in place using pegs, typically over a length of around 10 metres. An air pump is then used to inflate the canvas, giving it a curved, tunnel-like shape. Once the structure is formed, it is sprayed with water to activate the concrete.

After hydration, the material is left to set for 20 to 24 hours, during which it hardens into a solid structure. Finally, the completed storage area can be used for storing goods such as boxes.

Stage 4: Spreading on the ground. Shows a spread-out concrete canvas, 10 meters long, secured by "Pegs" at both ends.

* The process begins with the manufacturing of a multi-layered concrete canvas.
* The concrete canvas is delivered in rolls and then unwrapped and spread on the ground.
* Air is pumped into the canvas to form an arched structure.
* The structure is then hydrated with water and allowed to set for 20-24 hours.
* The final step involves using the hardened structure for storage.

title: Process: The diagram shows how tea leaves are processed into five tea types. Summarize th...
description: The diagram shows how tea leaves are processed into five tea types. Summarize the information by selecting and reporting the main features and make comparisons where relevant.
guide_html:
HƯỚNG DẪN VIẾT BÀI

How tea leaves are processed into five tea types

1. Giải thích đề

Sơ đồ mô tả quá trình chế biến lá trà để tạo ra 5 loại trà khác nhau.

→ Dạng: process (quy trình có phân nhánh)

2. Introduction (paraphrase)

Giữ:

  • tea leaves – processed – five types

Dùng:

  • shows → illustrates / outlines
  • process → procedure

Ví dụ:

The diagram illustrates how tea leaves are processed to produce five different types of tea.

3. Overview (ý chính)

  • Tất cả các loại trà đều trải qua các bước chung ban đầu:

leaf growth → plucking → withering

  • Sau đó, quy trình phân nhánh thành các phương pháp khác nhau
  • Sự khác biệt chính nằm ở:

steaming / rolling / crushing / mức độ fermentation

  • Tất cả kết thúc bằng oven drying

→ Ý: khác nhau ở xử lý trung gian → tạo ra các loại trà khác nhau

4. Chia BODY

BODY 1 – Giai đoạn chung & trà ít xử lý

Giai đoạn đầu (giống nhau):

  • Lá trà được:
  • trồng (growth)
  • hái (plucking)
  • làm héo (withering)

White tea:

  • Sau withering → đi thẳng đến drying

→ ít xử lý nhất

Green tea:

  • Sau withering → steaming
  • Sau đó:
  • rolling
  • drying

→ không có fermentation

BODY 2 – Trà lên men & xử lý mạnh hơn

Oolong tea:

  • After rolling → slight fermentation
  • Sau đó → drying

Black tea (2 loại):

  • Large-leaf black tea:
  • rolling → full fermentation → drying
  • Small-leaf black tea:
  • crushing (thay vì rolling)
  • → full fermentation
  • → drying

→ Ý: mức độ fermentation tăng dần từ oolong → black tea

5. Gợi ý từ vựng

  • undergo a process → trải qua quá trình
  • be subjected to → được xử lý bằng
  • fermentation → quá trình lên men
  • slight / full fermentation → lên men nhẹ / hoàn toàn
  • final stage → giai đoạn cuối
  • be dried in an oven → được sấy khô

The diagram illustrates how tea leaves are processed to produce five different types of tea.

Overall, all tea types follow the same initial stages—leaf growth, plucking, and withering—but differ in later processes such as steaming, rolling, fermentation, and crushing. The key differences lie in the level of fermentation, which determines the final type of tea.

After being harvested, the leaves are first withered to remove moisture. For green tea, the leaves are then steamed to prevent fermentation before being rolled and dried. In contrast, white tea undergoes minimal processing, as it is dried directly after withering without further treatment.

Oolong tea follows a more complex process: after rolling, the leaves undergo slight fermentation before oven drying. For black tea, the leaves are either rolled (for large-leaf black tea) or crushed (for small-leaf black tea), followed by full fermentation and final drying.
chart_description:
TYPE: process diagram
TITLE: How tea leaves are processed into five tea types
UNITS/AXES: Not applicable
SERIES/CATEGORIES:
White Tea: Light, delicate and mild
Green Tea: Fresh, grassy and refreshing
Oolong Tea: Balanced, floral and fragrant
Large Leaf Black Tea: Rich, full-bodied and smooth
Small Leaf Black Tea: Strong, brisk and robust
DATA:
1. Leaf Growth
2. Plucking
3. Wilting (Withering)
4. Steaming (for Green Tea)
5. Rolling (for White Tea, Green Tea, Oolong Tea, Large Leaf Black Tea)
6. Crushing (for Small Leaf Black Tea)
7. Slight Fermentation (for Oolong Tea)
8. Full Fermentation (for Large Leaf Black Tea, Small Leaf Black Tea)
9. Oven Drying (for all five tea types)
KEY FEATURES:
* All five types of tea begin with Leaf Growth, Plucking, Wilting (Withering), and end with Oven Drying.
* Green Tea is the only type that undergoes Steaming.
* White Tea is the only type that goes directly from Rolling to Oven Drying without fermentation.
* Oolong Tea undergoes Slight Fermentation, while Large Leaf Black Tea and Small Leaf Black Tea undergo Full Fermentation.
* Small Leaf Black Tea is distinguished by a Crushing step before Full Fermentation, unlike Large Leaf Black Tea which is Rolled.

HƯỚNG DẪN VIẾT BÀI

Pie charts: Book sales distribution (1972, 1992, 2012)

Giải thích đề

Ba biểu đồ tròn cho thấy tỷ lệ doanh số sách theo 5 thể loại (Adult Fiction, Children’s Fiction, Biography, Travel, Others) vào các năm 1972, 1992 và 2012.

→ Dạng: pie charts – so sánh nhiều mốc thời gian

Introduction (paraphrase)

Giữ các từ khóa:

book sales distribution

different categories

three years

Có thể dùng:

shows → illustrates / compares

distribution → proportion / breakdown

Mẫu:

The pie charts illustrate the distribution of book sales across five categories in 1972, 1992, and 2012.

Overview (ý chính)

Adult Fiction chiếm tỷ lệ lớn nhất và tăng mạnh theo thời gian

Children’s Fiction tăng nhẹ

Biography và Travel giảm đáng kể

Others giảm dần

→ xu hướng: thị trường ngày càng tập trung vào Adult Fiction, trong khi các thể loại khác mất dần thị phần

Từ khóa nên dùng:

accounted for the largest share

increased significantly

declined sharply

experienced a downward trend

BODY 1 – Nhóm chính (Adult Fiction, Children’s Fiction)

Adult Fiction:

20% → 25% → 45%

→ tăng mạnh, đặc biệt giai đoạn sau

Children’s Fiction:

20% → 22% → 25%

→ tăng nhẹ, ổn định

Ý chính: Fiction (đặc biệt Adult Fiction) ngày càng chiếm ưu thế trên thị trường

BODY 2 – Các nhóm còn lại (Biography, Travel, Others)

Biography:

20% → 15% → 8%

→ giảm đáng kể

Travel:

15% → 18% → 10%

→ tăng nhẹ rồi giảm mạnh

Others:

25% → 20% → 12%

→ giảm đều theo thời gian

Ý chính: các thể loại ngoài fiction nhìn chung suy giảm, đặc biệt Biography

Gợi ý từ vựng

account for

make up

rise dramatically

decline steadily

drop sharply

experience fluctuations

Ví dụ câu

Adult fiction accounted for the largest proportion and increased dramatically over the period.

Children’s fiction showed a gradual rise.

In contrast, the figure for biography declined significantly.

Travel experienced a slight increase before dropping sharply in 2012.

The proportion of other categories decreased steadily over time.

The three pie charts illustrate the distribution of book sales across five categories—adult fiction, children’s fiction, biography, travel, and others—in 1972, 1992, and 2012.

Overall, adult fiction increased substantially to become the dominant category by 2012, while biography and travel declined over time. In contrast, children’s fiction rose moderately, whereas the proportion of other books decreased steadily.

In 1972, sales were relatively evenly distributed, with “others” accounting for the largest share at 25%. Adult fiction represented 20%, equal to children’s fiction and biography, while travel made up the smallest proportion at 15%. By 1992, adult fiction had risen to 25%, becoming the leading category. Children’s fiction also increased slightly to 22%, whereas biography fell to 15%. Travel edged up to 18%, while the share of other books declined to 20%.

By 2012, adult fiction had grown markedly to 45%, far exceeding all other categories. Children’s fiction continued its upward trend, reaching 25%. In contrast, biography dropped sharply to just 8%, and travel decreased to 10%. The proportion of other books also fell significantly to 12%, indicating a clear shift in consumer preferences toward fiction, particularly adult titles.

Pie charts: Courses followed by students (1984–2004)

1. Giải thích đề

Ba biểu đồ tròn cho thấy tỷ lệ sinh viên theo học bốn loại khóa học (face-to-face, correspondence, mixed media, online) vào các năm 1984, 1994 và 2004.

courses followed

Online xuất hiện từ 1994 và duy trì ở mức thấp

Correspondence giảm nhẹ

→ xu hướng: chuyển dịch từ học trực tiếp sang các hình thức linh hoạt hơn

4. BODY 1 – Face-to-face & Mixed media

Face-to-face:

→ giảm liên tục

→ tăng mạnh

account for

make up

remain relatively low

The three pie charts illustrate the proportions of students taking four types of courses—face-to-face, correspondence, mixed media, and online—in 1984, 1994 and 2004.

Overall, face-to-face courses were the dominant mode at the beginning of the period but declined steadily over time, while mixed media courses rose significantly to become the most popular by 2004. Meanwhile, online learning emerged only in 1994 and remained a relatively small segment, and correspondence courses showed a slight downward trend.

In 1984, traditional face-to-face courses accounted for a substantial majority at 67%. Correspondence courses made up 20%, while mixed media courses represented a smaller share at 13%. There was no participation in online courses at this point.

By 1994, the proportion of face-to-face learning had fallen to 54%, although it still remained the largest category. Mixed media courses increased modestly to 15%, matching the share of correspondence courses, which stayed unchanged at 20%. Notably, online courses appeared for the first time, accounting for 11% of all enrolments.

In 2004, the trend shifted further. Face-to-face courses declined sharply to 40%, while mixed media courses rose markedly to 35%, becoming nearly as popular as traditional learning. Correspondence courses decreased slightly to 15%, and online courses remained relatively limited at 10%, showing only marginal change since 1994.

3. Overview (ý chính)

Dinner chiếm tỷ lệ cao nhất về sodium và saturated fat

Snacks chiếm tỷ lệ cao nhất về added sugar

→ xu hướng: bữa tối và đồ ăn vặt đóng góp nhiều nhất vào các chất không lành mạnh

account for

make up

be highest in

constitute

The three pie charts illustrate the average proportions of sodium, saturated fat and added sugar contained in four typical meals—breakfast, lunch, dinner and snacks—in the USA.

Overall, dinner contributes the highest share of sodium and saturated fat, whereas added sugar is predominantly consumed in snacks. By contrast, breakfast consistently accounts for the smallest proportions across all three nutrients.

In terms of sodium, dinner makes up the largest proportion at 43%, followed by lunch at 29%, while both breakfast and snacks contribute equally at 14% each. A similar pattern is observed for saturated fat, with dinner again the highest at 37%, and lunch representing 26%. Snacks account for 21%, whereas breakfast has the lowest share at 16%.

By comparison, added sugar is mainly consumed through snacks, which constitute a substantial 42%. Dinner and lunch contribute more moderate proportions, at 23% and 19% respectively, while breakfast remains the lowest at 16%. This indicates a clear shift in dietary patterns, with sugar intake concentrated outside main meals, unlike sodium and fat, which are primarily associated with dinner.

HƯỚNG DẪN VIẾT BÀI

Pie charts: Electricity production sources (India, Sweden, Morocco, Vietnam)

1. Giải thích đề

Bốn biểu đồ tròn cho thấy tỷ lệ sản xuất điện từ ba nguồn (fossil fuel, hydro power, nuclear power) ở bốn quốc gia: Ấn Độ, Thụy Điển, Morocco và Việt Nam.

The pie charts illustrate the proportions of electricity production from different sources in four countries.

3. Overview (ý chính)

Fossil fuel chiếm ưu thế ở Ấn Độ và Việt Nam

Hydro power là nguồn chính ở Morocco và Sweden

Nuclear power chỉ đáng kể ở Sweden và rất thấp hoặc không có ở các nước còn lại

→ xu hướng: các quốc gia có cơ cấu năng lượng rất khác nhau

4. BODY 1 – India & Vietnam

India:

Fossil fuel: 82% → cao nhất

Hydro: 14%

Nuclear: 4%

Vietnam:

Fossil fuel: 56% → cao nhất

Hydro: 44%

Nuclear: 0%

→ Ý chính: hai nước phụ thuộc nhiều vào fossil fuel

5. BODY 2 – Sweden & Morocco

Sweden:

Hydro: 52% → cao nhất

Nuclear: 44%

Fossil fuel: 4%

Morocco:

Hydro: 95% → áp đảo

Fossil fuel: 5%

Nuclear: 0%

→ Ý chính: Sweden đa dạng hơn, Morocco phụ thuộc gần như hoàn toàn vào hydro

6. Gợi ý từ vựng

account for

make up

dominate

be the primary source

have a negligible share

be heavily reliant on

The four pie charts illustrate the proportions of electricity generated from fossil fuels, hydro power and nuclear power in India, Sweden, Morocco and Vietnam between 2003 and 2008.

Overall, the dominant energy source varied markedly across countries. Fossil fuels accounted for the vast majority of electricity production in India and Vietnam, whereas hydro power was the primary source in Morocco and Sweden. Nuclear energy was only significant in Sweden and made a negligible or non-existent contribution in the other countries.

In India, electricity generation was heavily dependent on fossil fuels, which made up 82% of total production. Hydro power contributed a relatively small share at 14%, while nuclear energy accounted for just 4%. A similar reliance on fossil fuels can be seen in Vietnam, although to a lesser extent, with 56% of electricity derived from this source. The remaining 44% came entirely from hydro power, with no contribution from nuclear energy.

By contrast, Morocco relied almost exclusively on hydro power, which represented 95% of its electricity generation. Fossil fuels made up only 5%, and nuclear power was not used at all. Sweden displayed the most balanced energy mix among the four countries. Hydro power was the largest contributor at 52%, followed closely by nuclear energy at 44%, while fossil fuels accounted for a minimal 4%.

guide_html:
ELTS Writing Task 1 – Energy production by resource (pie charts)

TID sẽ chỉ bạn cách xử lý dạng double pie chart này sao cho overview rõ và không bị liệt kê số liệu nha.

1. Hiểu đề bài

Biểu đồ cho thấy tỷ lệ sản xuất năng lượng từ 6 nguồn khác nhau:

  • Hydrogen
  • Natural gas
  • Oil
  • Other renewable
  • Coal
  • Nuclear

trong hai năm:

  • 1985
  • 2003

TID nhắc bạn:

Với pie chart theo thời gian, bạn cần tập trung vào:

  • nguồn lớn nhất / nhỏ nhất
  • nguồn tăng mạnh
  • nguồn giảm mạnh
  • sự thay đổi tổng thể giữa 2 năm

2. Cách viết Introduction

Paraphrase:

  • energy production
  • by different resources
  • in 1985 and 2003

Viết 1 câu ngắn gọn là đủ nha.

3. Cách viết Overview

TID gợi ý overview như này:

  • Natural gas remained the largest source in both years
  • Oil and coal increased significantly over the period
  • Nuclear energy declined considerably
  • Hydrogen stayed unchanged and other renewable sources remained relatively small

TID lưu ý:

Overview chỉ cần:

  • biggest
  • xu hướng chính
  • nguồn tăng / giảm nổi bật

Không cần nhét quá nhiều số nha.

4. Cách chia Body

BODY 1 – Major energy sources

Tập trung vào:

  • Natural gas
  • Oil
  • Coal

TID gợi ý:

Đây là các nguồn chiếm tỷ lệ lớn nhất nên viết trước.

Natural gas:

  • giảm từ 52% → 39%
  • nhưng vẫn đứng đầu

Oil:

  • tăng đáng kể từ 13% → 23%

Coal:

  • tăng mạnh từ 8% → 22%

TID lưu ý:

Coal và oil là 2 nguồn tăng nổi bật nhất nha.

BODY 2 – Remaining sources

Hydrogen:

  • giữ nguyên 4%

Other renewable:

  • tăng nhẹ từ 1% → 4%

Nuclear:

  • giảm mạnh từ 22% → 8%

TID gợi ý:

Body này nên nhấn mạnh:

  • nuclear giảm đáng kể
  • renewable tăng nhưng vẫn thấp

5. Những điểm nên highlight

TID gợi ý vài ý dễ ăn điểm:

  • Natural gas remained dominant despite a decline
  • Coal almost tripled
  • Oil nearly doubled
  • Nuclear dropped sharply
  • Renewable sources still accounted for only a small proportion in 2003

The two pie charts compare the proportions of energy production from six different resources in 1985 and 2003.

Overall, natural gas remained the dominant source of energy production in both years, despite a noticeable decline over the period. By contrast, coal and oil experienced significant growth, while nuclear energy saw a substantial decrease. Hydrogen remained unchanged, and other renewable sources continued to account for relatively small percentages.

In 1985, natural gas was by far the largest energy source, representing 52% of total production. Nuclear energy accounted for 22%, making it the second most important resource, while oil contributed 13%. Coal made up a relatively modest proportion at 8%, whereas hydrogen and other renewable sources represented only 4% and 1% respectively.

By 2003, the proportion of energy generated from natural gas had fallen to 39%, although it still remained the leading source. Oil and coal both increased considerably, rising to 23% and 22% respectively. In contrast, nuclear energy declined sharply to just 8%. Hydrogen remained stable at 4%, while the figure for other renewable resources rose slightly to 4%.

Pie charts: Australian household energy use vs greenhouse gas emissions

1. Giải thích đề

3. Overview (ý chính)

Refrigeration và lighting tạo ra tỷ lệ phát thải cao hơn so với mức tiêu thụ năng lượng

Cooling chiếm tỷ lệ nhỏ nhất

→ xu hướng: mức tiêu thụ năng lượng không tương ứng trực tiếp với lượng khí thải

4. BODY 1 – Energy use

Lighting: 8%

Cooling: 3% → thấp nhất

→ Ý chính: emissions tập trung vào water heating và appliances

6. Gợi ý từ vựng

account for

make up

contribute to

be responsible for

be disproportionately high/low

in contrast

The two pie charts compare the proportions of energy use in Australian households and the corresponding shares of greenhouse gas emissions by end use.

Overall, heating accounts for the largest share of energy consumption, whereas water heating is the biggest contributor to emissions. Notably, most other categories generate a higher proportion of emissions relative to the energy they consume, except for heating.

In terms of energy use, heating dominates at 42%, followed by water heating at 30%. Other appliances account for 15%, while refrigeration and lighting represent relatively small shares at 7% and 4%, respectively.

By contrast, water heating is the leading source of greenhouse gas emissions at 32%, closely followed by other appliances at 28%. Refrigeration contributes 14%, which is double its share of energy use, and lighting also produces a higher proportion of emissions (8%) compared to its energy consumption. Cooling, although not significant in energy use, accounts for 3% of emissions. Meanwhile, heating produces only 15% of emissions despite being the largest consumer of energy, indicating it is comparatively less emission-intensive.

HƯỚNG DẪN VIẾT BÀI

Pie charts: Study modes in three countries (2010 vs 2015)

1. Giải thích đề

Sáu biểu đồ tròn cho thấy tỷ lệ ba hình thức học (Evening class, Online, Abroad) ở ba quốc gia (A, B, C) vào năm 2010 và 2015.

→ Dạng: pie charts – nhiều đối tượng \+ nhiều mốc thời gian

2. Introduction (paraphrase)

Giữ các từ khóa:

study modes

three countries

two years

Có thể dùng:

shows → illustrates / compares

proportions → distribution

Mẫu:

The pie charts illustrate the distribution of three study modes in three different countries in 2010 and 2015.

3. Overview (ý chính)

Evening classes chiếm tỷ lệ lớn nhất ở tất cả các quốc gia nhưng giảm theo thời gian

Online tăng mạnh, đặc biệt ở Country B và C

Abroad nhìn chung giảm hoặc chiếm tỷ lệ nhỏ

→ xu hướng: chuyển dịch từ học truyền thống sang học online

4. BODY 1 – Country A

Evening class:

70% → 67%

→ giảm nhẹ

Abroad:

25% → 23%

→ giảm nhẹ

Online:

5% → 10%

→ tăng gấp đôi

→ Ý chính: thay đổi nhỏ, online bắt đầu tăng

5. BODY 2 – Country B

Evening class:

72% → 48%

→ giảm mạnh

Online:

8% → 32%

→ tăng đáng kể

Abroad:

20% → 20%

→ không đổi

→ Ý chính: chuyển dịch rõ rệt sang học online

6. BODY 3 – Country C

Evening class:

94% → 82%

→ vẫn chiếm ưu thế nhưng giảm

Online:

6% → 15%

→ tăng rõ

Abroad:

0% → 3%

→ xuất hiện nhưng rất nhỏ

→ Ý chính: vẫn phụ thuộc vào học truyền thống nhưng có xu hướng đa dạng hóa

The six pie charts compare how students in three countries (A, B and C) participated in evening classes, online courses and study abroad in 2010 and 2015.

Overall, evening classes remained the dominant mode in all three countries, although their shares declined over time, particularly in Country B and C. Meanwhile, online learning increased markedly across all countries, whereas studying abroad showed mixed trends.

In Country A, evening classes accounted for the majority in both years, though this figure fell slightly from 70% in 2010 to 67% in 2015. Online learning doubled from 5% to 10%, while participation in studying abroad decreased marginally from 25% to 23%.

A more dramatic shift occurred in Country B. While evening classes dominated in 2010 at 72%, this proportion dropped sharply to 48% by 2015. In contrast, online learning rose significantly from 8% to 32%, becoming a major mode of study. The proportion of students studying abroad remained unchanged at 20%.

Country C showed a similar pattern to Country B, though less pronounced. Evening classes declined from an overwhelming 94% in 2010 to 82% in 2015. Online participation more than doubled from 6% to 15%, whereas the proportion studying abroad fell from a negligible level to just 3% in 2015.
chart_description:
TYPE: pie chart
TITLE: (none)
UNITS/AXES: percentages, years 2010 and 2015
SERIES/CATEGORIES: Country A, Country B, Country C, Evening Class, Online, Abroad
DATA:
Country A 2010: Evening Class 70%, Online 5%, Abroad 25%
Country A 2015: Evening Class 67%, Online 10%, Abroad 23%
Country B 2010: Evening Class 72%, Online 8%, Abroad 20%
Country B 2015: Evening Class 48%, Online 32%, Abroad 20%
Country C 2010: Evening Class 94%, Online 6%, Abroad 0%
Country C 2015: Evening Class 82%, Online 15%, Abroad 3%
KEY FEATURES:
*   In 2010, Evening Class was the most popular option in all three countries, ranging from 70% to 94%.
*   By 2015, Evening Class decreased in popularity across all countries, most significantly in Country B (from 72% to 48%).
*   Online learning increased in popularity in all three countries from 2010 to 2015, with the largest increase in Country B (from 8% to 32%).
*   Studying Abroad remained constant in Country B (20%) and slightly decreased in Country A (from 25% to 23%).
*   Country C had no students studying Abroad in 2010, but this increased to 3% in 2015.
*   Country C consistently had the highest percentage of students attending Evening Class in both years (94% in 2010, 82% in 2015).

guide_html:
HƯỚNG DẪN VIẾT BÀI

Pie charts: Reasons for immigrants to and from a European country (2009)

1. Giải thích đề

Hai biểu đồ tròn cho thấy lý do người nhập cư đến và rời khỏi một quốc gia châu Âu vào năm 2009.

→ Dạng: pie charts – so sánh 2 biểu đồ khác đối tượng

2. Introduction (paraphrase)

Giữ các từ khóa:

reasons for immigrants

to and from

a European country

Có thể dùng:

shows → illustrates / compares

reasons → purposes

Mẫu:

The pie charts illustrate the reasons why people immigrated to and emigrated from a European country in 2009.

3. Overview (ý chính)

Có việc làm chắc chắn là lý do phổ biến nhất ở cả hai nhóm

Tỷ lệ này cao hơn đáng kể ở người rời đi

Study và accompany/family phổ biến hơn ở người đến

No reason chiếm tỷ lệ nhỏ nhất ở cả hai

→ xu hướng: việc làm là động lực chính, nhưng mục đích khác nhau giữa hai nhóm

4. BODY 1 – Immigrants to the country

Definite job: 23%

Accompany/Family: 25% → cao nhất

Look for job: 15%

Study: 15%

Other reasons: 15%

No reason: 7% → thấp nhất

→ Ý chính: lý do khá phân tán, với family là cao nhất

5. BODY 2 – Immigrants from the country

Definite job: 38% → cao nhất

Other reasons: 23%

Accompany/Family: 15%

Look for job: 13%

Study: 7%

No reason: 4% → thấp nhất

→ Ý chính: rời đi chủ yếu vì công việc

6. Gợi ý từ vựng

account for

make up

be the main reason

be more/less common

represent

constitute

The two pie charts illustrate the main reasons for immigrants moving to and from a European country in 2009.

Overall, employment-related reasons were the dominant factor in both directions, particularly among those leaving the country. In contrast, study and family-related motives were more significant for incoming migrants.

For immigration to the country, the largest proportion of people moved for a definite job, accounting for 23%. This was followed by those accompanying family members at 25%, which slightly exceeded the figure for employment. Three other categories—looking for a job, studying, and other reasons—each represented an equal share of 15%, while only 7% migrated with no specific reason.

By comparison, for emigration, having a definite job was by far the most common reason, rising markedly to 38%. Other reasons also increased to 23%, making it the second-largest category. The proportion of people accompanying family members stood at 15%, whereas those leaving to look for work accounted for 13%. Study was a relatively minor factor at 7%, and only 4% of individuals left without a clear reason.

TYPE: pie chart
TITLE: Reasons for immigrants to a European Country in 2009; Reasons for immigrants from a European Country in 2009
UNITS/AXES: Percentages
SERIES/CATEGORIES: Definite job, Look for job, Study, Accompany/Family, Other reasons, No reason
DATA:
Reasons for immigrants to a European Country in 2009:
Definite job: 23%
Look for job: 15%
Study: 15%
Accompany/Family: 25%
Other reasons: 15%
No reason: 7%

Reasons for immigrants from a European Country in 2009:
Definite job: 38%
Look for job: 13%
Study: 7%
Accompany/Family: 15%
Other reasons: 23%
No reason: 4%
KEY FEATURES:
*   For immigrants to a European country, "Accompany/Family" was the largest reason at 25%.
*   For immigrants from a European country, "Definite job" was the largest reason at 38%.
*   "No reason" was the smallest category for both types of immigrants, at 7% for immigrants to and 4% for immigrants from.
*   The percentage of people moving for a "Definite job" was significantly higher for those leaving a European country (38%) compared to those arriving (23%).
*   "Other reasons" accounted for 15% of immigrants to a European country and 23% of immigrants from a European country.
*   "Study" was a more common reason for immigrants to a European country (15%) than for immigrants from a European country (7%).

guide_html:
HƯỚNG DẪN VIẾT BÀI

Pie charts: Reasons for library visits (1991 vs 2000)

1. Giải thích đề

Hai biểu đồ tròn cho thấy lý do người dân đến thư viện vào năm 1991 và 2000, với tổng số lượt là 290 triệu mỗi năm.

→ Dạng: pie charts – so sánh 2 mốc thời gian

2. Introduction (paraphrase)

Giữ các từ khóa:

library visits

reasons

two years

Có thể dùng:

shows → illustrates / compares

reasons → purposes

Mẫu:

The pie charts illustrate the reasons why people visited libraries in 1991 and 2000.

3. Overview (ý chính)

Borrowing/returning books chiếm tỷ lệ lớn nhất ở cả hai năm nhưng giảm

Obtaining information tăng đáng kể

Study giảm rõ rệt

Reading (newspapers/magazines) tăng nhẹ

Xuất hiện thêm borrowing videos vào năm 2000

→ xu hướng: thư viện chuyển từ chức năng truyền thống sang cung cấp thông tin nhiều hơn

4. BODY 1 – Nhóm chính (Borrow books, Obtain information)

Borrow or return books:

65% → 55%

→ giảm nhưng vẫn lớn nhất

Obtain information:

10% → 20%

→ tăng mạnh, gấp đôi

→ Ý chính: vai trò của việc tìm kiếm thông tin ngày càng quan trọng

5. BODY 2 – Các hoạt động còn lại

Study:

10% → 5%

→ giảm một nửa

Read newspapers/magazines:

15% → 18%

→ tăng nhẹ

Borrow or return videos:

0% → 2%

→ xuất hiện mới

→ Ý chính: các hoạt động học tập giảm, trong khi giải trí/thông tin tăng

The two pie charts compare how visitors used a library in 1991 and 2000, with the total number of visits remaining unchanged at 290 million in both years.

Overall, borrowing or returning books remained the primary purpose in both years, although its share declined slightly. In contrast, obtaining information became significantly more common, while studying decreased. New activity in the form of borrowing or returning videos appeared in 2000.

In 1991, a substantial 65% of visitors went to the library to borrow or return books, making it by far the dominant activity. Reading newspapers or magazines accounted for 15%, while both studying and obtaining information each represented 10% of visits.

By 2000, the proportion of visitors borrowing or returning books had fallen to 55%, though it still remained the largest category. Obtaining information doubled to 20%, becoming the second most common purpose. Reading newspapers or magazines increased slightly to 18%. In contrast, studying declined sharply to just 5%. Additionally, borrowing or returning videos emerged as a new activity, accounting for a small proportion of 2%.

* The total number of visits remained constant at 290 million in both years.
* "Borrow or return books" was the most popular reason for visiting the library in both years, though it decreased from 65% to 55%.
* "Obtain information" doubled from 10% to 20%.
* "Study" decreased by half from 10% to 5%.
* "Read newspaper or magazine" saw a slight increase from 15% to 18%.
* "Borrow or return videos" was a new category in 2000, accounting for 2% of visits.

title: Pie Chart: The pie charts show people’s reasons for immigration to a European country in 20...
description: The pie charts show people’s reasons for immigration to a European country in 2009 and reasons for emigration from a European country in 200
guide_html:
Hướng dẫn viết bài

IELTS Writing Task 1 – Reasons for immigration (pie charts)

TID sẽ chỉ bạn cách xử lý dạng double pie chart này sao cho overview rõ ý và body không bị kể số liệu nha.

1. Hiểu đề bài

Biểu đồ cho thấy:

  • lý do nhập cư vào một quốc gia châu Âu
  • và lý do rời khỏi quốc gia đó

trong năm 2009.

TID nhắc bạn:

Với pie chart, điều quan trọng nhất là:

  • tìm category lớn nhất
  • nhỏ nhất
  • nhóm nào giống nhau
  • điểm khác biệt nổi bật giữa 2 biểu đồ

2. Cách viết Introduction

Paraphrase:

  • reasons for immigration / emigration
  • a European country
  • in 2009

Viết 1 câu ngắn là đủ nha.

3. Cách viết Overview

TID gợi ý overview nên tập trung vào:

  • Job-related reasons chiếm tỷ lệ lớn nhất ở cả hai charts
  • “No reason” là thấp nhất
  • People leaving the country có xu hướng đi vì “definite job” nhiều hơn
  • Chart “from the country” có sự chênh lệch lớn hơn giữa các categories

TID lưu ý:

Overview chỉ cần:

  • biggest
  • smallest
  • xu hướng chung
  • 1 điểm khác biệt nổi bật

Không cần nhiều số liệu nha.

4. Cách chia Body

BODY 1 – Immigration TO the country

Nhóm:

  • category lớn nhất
  • các nhóm bằng nhau
  • category nhỏ nhất

TID gợi ý:

Chart này khá balanced nên có thể:

  • viết largest category trước
  • gom 3 categories bằng nhau vào cùng 1 câu
  • kết thúc bằng smallest category

BODY 2 – Immigration FROM the country

Tập trung vào:

  • “Definite job” vượt trội rõ rệt
  • các category trung bình
  • smallest category

TID lưu ý:

Body 2 nên nhấn mạnh:

  • sự dominance của “definite job”
  • một vài categories giảm so với chart đầu

5. Những điểm nên so sánh

TID gợi ý vài ý so sánh dễ ăn điểm:

  • Definite job tăng mạnh ở chart “from”
  • Study giảm đáng kể
  • Accompany/family giảm
  • No reason luôn thấp nhất
  • Employment-related purposes chiếm phần lớn ở cả hai charts

6. Gợi ý paraphrase

TID gợi ý một số cách diễn đạt:

  • accounted for
  • represented
  • made up
  • the largest proportion
  • a relatively small percentage
  • employment-related reasons
  • people migrating for work
  • by comparison
  • whereas / while

TID lưu ý:

Pie chart không cần viết quá nhiều số.

Quan trọng là:

  • grouping thông minh
  • overview rõ
  • so sánh có chọn lọc nha.

The two pie charts illustrate the reasons why people immigrated to and emigrated from a European country in 2009.

Overall, employment-related reasons accounted for the largest proportions in both charts, particularly having a definite job. By contrast, migrating without a specific reason represented the smallest percentage in each case. In addition, people leaving the country were more likely to move for a definite job than those entering it.

Regarding immigration to the European country, accompanying family members was the most common reason, accounting for 25% of immigrants. This was followed closely by people who moved for a definite job at 23%. Meanwhile, study, looking for work and other reasons each represented an identical figure of 15%. Only a small minority of immigrants, at 7%, moved without giving a particular reason.

As for emigration from the country, having a definite job became significantly more dominant, making up 38% of all cases. Other reasons accounted for 23%, while accompanying family represented 15%. The proportion of people leaving to look for work stood at 13%, compared to just 7% for study purposes. Similar to the first chart, no reason was the least common category, at only 4%.

TYPE: pie chart
TITLE: Reasons For Immigrants To A European Country In 2009
UNITS/AXES: Percentages, 2009
SERIES/CATEGORIES: No reason, Other Reasons, Accompany/Family, Study, Look For Job, Definite Job
DATA:
No reason: 7%
Other Reasons: 15%
Accompany/Family: 25%
Study: 15%
Look For Job: 15%
Definite Job: 23%

TYPE: pie chart
TITLE: Reasons For Immigrants From A European Country In 2009

DATA:

Accompany/Family: 15%
Study: 7%
Look For Job: 13%
Definite Job: 38%

title: Pie Chart: The charts below show the proportion of holidaymakers using four different types...

guide_html:
HƯỚNG DẪN VIẾT BÀI

Pie charts: Holiday accommodation (1988, 1998, 2008)

1. Giải thích đề

Ba biểu đồ tròn cho thấy tỷ lệ các loại hình lưu trú khi đi nghỉ (staying with family, rented apartment, camping, hotels) vào các năm 1988, 1998 và 2008.

→ Dạng: pie charts – nhiều mốc thời gian

2. Introduction (paraphrase)

Giữ các từ khóa:

holiday accommodation

different types

three years

Có thể dùng:

shows → illustrates / compares

types → categories

Mẫu:

The pie charts illustrate the distribution of different types of holiday accommodation in 1988, 1998 and 2008.

3. Overview (ý chính)

Staying with family chiếm tỷ lệ lớn nhất ở cả ba năm nhưng giảm vào 2008

Rented apartment tăng mạnh và trở thành lựa chọn phổ biến hơn

Camping giảm dần

Hotels tăng nhẹ rồi ổn định

→ xu hướng: chuyển từ ở với gia đình sang thuê căn hộ

4. BODY 1 – Staying with family & Rented apartment

Staying with family:

52% → 54% → 44%

→ cao nhất nhưng giảm vào giai đoạn cuối

Rented apartment:

7% → 11% → 22%

→ tăng mạnh, đặc biệt đến 2008

→ Ý chính: sự gia tăng rõ rệt của hình thức thuê căn hộ

5. BODY 2 – Camping & Hotels

Camping:

26% → 13% → 12%

→ giảm đáng kể

Hotels:

15% → 22% → 22%

→ tăng rồi giữ nguyên

→ Ý chính: camping mất dần phổ biến, hotels ổn định

6. Gợi ý từ vựng

account for

make up

increase steadily

decline significantly

remain stable

become more popular

The three pie charts illustrate the proportions of tourists choosing four types of accommodation—staying with family, rented apartments, camping and hotels—in 1988, 1998 and 2008.

Overall, staying with family was consistently the most popular option across the period, although its share declined slightly by 2008. In contrast, rented apartments became increasingly popular, while camping experienced a steady decrease. The proportion of tourists staying in hotels rose initially and then remained stable.

In 1988, over half of tourists (52%) stayed with family, making it by far the dominant choice. Camping was the second most common option at 26%, followed by hotels at 15%. Only a small minority, 7%, chose rented apartments.

By 1998, the proportion of those staying with family increased marginally to 54%, while hotel use rose to 22%. Meanwhile, camping dropped significantly to 13%. Rented apartments saw a modest increase to 11%, though they remained the least preferred option.

In 2008, staying with family declined to 44%, though it still ranked first. Rented apartments, however, doubled from the previous figure to 22%, equalling the proportion for hotels, which remained unchanged at 22%. Camping continued its downward trend, falling slightly further to 12%.
chart_description:
TYPE: pie chart
TITLE: none
UNITS/AXES: Percentages, Years: 1988, 1998, 2008
SERIES/CATEGORIES: Staying with family, Rented apartment, Camping, Hotels
DATA:

Camping: 26%

KEY FEATURES:
* "Staying with family" was the most popular accommodation type in all three years, though its percentage decreased by 8% from 1998 to 2008.
* "Rented apartment" saw a steady increase in popularity, more than tripling its share from 7% in 1988 to 22% in 2008.
* "Camping" experienced a significant decline, dropping from 26% in 1988 to 12% in 2008.
* "Hotels" increased from 15% in 1988 to 22% in 1998, and then remained stable at 22% in 2008.
* In 2008, "Rented apartment" and "Hotels" shared the same percentage of popularity at 22%.

title: Pie Chart: The charts below show the percentage of students at an adult education centre ta...
description: The charts below show the percentage of students at an adult education centre taking various courses offered in 1985 and this year. Summaris
guide_html:
Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.

HƯỚNG DẪN VIẾT BÀI

Pie charts: Course enrolment comparison (1985 vs Current year)

1. Giải thích đề

Hai biểu đồ tròn so sánh tỷ lệ đăng ký các khóa học vào năm 1985 và hiện tại.

→ Dạng: pie charts – so sánh 2 thời điểm (có thay đổi danh mục)

2. Introduction (paraphrase)

Giữ các từ khóa:

course enrolment

comparison

two time periods

Có thể dùng:

shows → illustrates / compares

enrolment → participation

Mẫu:

The pie charts illustrate the distribution of course enrolments in 1985 and in the current year.

3. Overview (ý chính)

Fitness and dance giữ nguyên tỷ lệ

IT xuất hiện và trở thành lớn nhất

Modern languages giảm

Cookery tăng

Một số môn biến mất (music appreciation, local history)

Từ khóa nên dùng:

remained unchanged

emerged as the largest category

declined

increased

disappeared

4. Chia BODY

BODY 1 – Các môn giữ hoặc tăng

Fitness and dance:

22% → 22% (không đổi)

Cookery:

14% → 19% (tăng)

Art:

17% → 15% (giảm nhẹ)

IT:

không có năm 1985 → 27% (cao nhất hiện tại)

Ý chính: IT trở thành môn phổ biến nhất, cookery tăng, fitness ổn định

BODY 2 – Các môn giảm hoặc biến mất

Modern languages:

24% → 17% (giảm đáng kể)

Music appreciation & Local history:

8% \+ 15% (1985) → không còn trong năm hiện tại

Ý chính: một số môn truyền thống giảm hoặc biến mất, cho thấy sự thay đổi sở thích học tập

5. Gợi ý từ vựng

account for

make up

increase moderately

decline significantly

remain stable

be replaced by

emerge as

Ví dụ:

IT emerged as the largest category in the current year.

Fitness and dance remained unchanged over time.

Modern languages declined significantly.

Some subjects were replaced by newer courses such as IT.

The two pie charts compare course enrolment in 1985 and the current year across several subjects.

Overall, while fitness and dance maintained its position as one of the most popular courses, there was a clear shift towards technology-related study, with IT becoming the dominant subject in the current year. In contrast, traditional subjects such as local history and music appreciation disappeared entirely.

In 1985, modern languages accounted for the largest proportion of enrolments at 24%, followed by fitness and dance at 22%. Art represented 17%, while cookery made up 14%. Local history and music appreciation were less popular, at 15% and 8% respectively.

In the current year, IT has emerged as the most popular course, comprising 27% of enrolments. Cookery increased to 19%, while fitness and dance remained unchanged at 22%. Art declined slightly to 15%, and modern languages fell to 17%. Notably, local history and music appreciation are no longer present in the distribution.
chart_description:
TYPE: pie chart
TITLE: Course enrollment comparison: 1985 vs Current Year
UNITS/AXES: Percentages
SERIES/CATEGORIES:
1985: Art, Fitness and dance, Cookery, Music appreciation, Local history, Modern languages (French German Spanish)
Current year: Art, Fitness and dance, Cookery, IT, Modern languages (French German Spanish)
DATA:
1985:
Art: 17%
Fitness and dance: 22%
Cookery: 14%
Music appreciation: 8%

The two pie charts illustrate the distribution of the world’s forest area across five regions and the proportion of global timber production originating from these regions.

Overall, Africa contains the largest share of global forest, whereas North America is the leading producer of timber. In contrast, Africa contributes a disproportionately small share of timber despite its extensive forest coverage.

In terms of forest distribution, Africa accounts for the highest proportion at 27%, followed by North America at 25%. Europe represents 18% of global forest area, while South America and Asia contribute 16% and 14% respectively, making Asia the region with the smallest forest share.

However, the pattern for timber production differs considerably. North America dominates with 30% of global timber output, despite having a slightly smaller forest area than Africa. South America is the second-largest producer at 23%, followed by Europe and Asia at 20% and 18% respectively. Notably, Africa contributes only 9% of timber production, which is significantly lower than its share of forest resources.

Petroleum products generated the highest revenue in both years, rising slightly from about $60 billion in 2015 to roughly $62 billion in 2016. Earnings from engineered goods also increased, from approximately $56 billion to $60 billion. In contrast, gems and jewellery experienced a decline, falling from around $42 billion to $40 billion.

Agricultural products saw a marginal increase, from about $29 billion in 2015 to just over $30 billion in 2016. The most notable growth was in textiles, which rose significantly from roughly $25 billion to about $30 billion.

In terms of percentage change, textiles recorded the largest increase at 15.24%, followed by engineered goods at 8.5%. Petroleum products grew modestly by 3%, while agricultural products saw only a slight rise of 0.81%. Gems and jewellery was the only category to decrease, with a drop of 5.18%.

The two pie charts compare how people allocated their daily time across six activities in 1958 and 2008.

Overall, working and sleeping accounted for the largest shares in both years, although the proportion of time spent working increased markedly, while sleeping and commuting declined. Meanwhile, leisure-related activities showed relatively minor changes.

In 1958, working occupied the largest proportion of the day at 33%, closely followed by sleeping at 32%. Travelling to work made up 19%, while relaxing at home accounted for 8%. Smaller proportions were devoted to going out (6%) and other activities such as hobbies or sport (2%).

By 2008, the proportion of time spent working had risen significantly to 42%, making it by far the dominant activity. In contrast, sleeping decreased to 25%, and commuting fell to 13%. Relaxing at home declined slightly to 6%, while the figure for going out remained unchanged at 6%. Notably, time spent on other activities increased fourfold to 8%.

The table and bar chart compare the percentage increase and the number of mobile phone connections per 1,000 people in five countries between 2001 and 2002.

All countries experienced growth, although the scale differed considerably. The USA and South Korea recorded much higher connection levels than the other nations, while Britain showed the most significant relative increase.

In terms of percentage change, Britain rose most sharply, with an increase of 230%. The USA also saw substantial growth at 170%, followed by Switzerland at 120%. Germany experienced a more moderate rise of 80%, whereas South Korea had the smallest increase, at just 20%.

Looking at the actual figures, the USA had the highest number of connections, climbing from 93 per 1,000 people in 2001 to about 251 in 2002. South Korea also maintained a high level, increasing from 122 to roughly 134. By contrast, the remaining countries had relatively low figures. Switzerland grew from approximately 3.6 to nearly 8, while Germany rose from about 3.4 to 5.6. Britain, despite its rapid growth, only increased from around 3.3 to just under 11 connections per 1,000 people.

account for

make up

be the most common mode

be heavily reliant on

be significantly higher/lower

in contrast

The pie chart and bar chart illustrate average commuting times in the UK and the modes of transport used by workers in London and the rest of the UK in 2009.

Overall, most workers had relatively short commutes, with journeys under 30 minutes accounting for the majority. In terms of transport, cars were by far the most common mode outside London, whereas London commuters relied more heavily on public transport, particularly trains and the underground.

Regarding commuting time, the largest proportion of workers (42%) travelled for just 1–15 minutes. A further 33% had journeys lasting 16–30 minutes, meaning that three-quarters of workers commuted for under half an hour. Longer journeys were far less common, with 12% travelling for 31–45 minutes, 8% for 45–60 minutes, and only 5% commuting for over an hour.

In terms of transport modes, car use dominated in the rest of the UK, accounting for just over 70% of commuters, compared to around 35% in London. Walking was relatively similar in both areas, at approximately 18% in London and 20% elsewhere. Bus usage was slightly higher in London (about 23%) than in the rest of the country (around 17%). By contrast, rail-based transport showed the greatest difference: trains were used by roughly 29% of London workers but only about 2% outside the capital, while the underground was used by around 27% in London and was negligible elsewhere. Cycling remained the least common mode in both regions, at roughly 3–4%.

The bar chart compares the number of tourists from the UK, the USA and Japan who visited Australia in 1995 and 2005, while the line graph shows changes in accommodation types over the same period.

Overall, visitor numbers from the UK and the USA increased significantly over the decade, whereas the figure for Japan declined. In terms of accommodation, staying in hotels was more popular initially, but backpacking grew steadily and matched hotel stays by 2005.

Looking first at tourist numbers, arrivals from the UK rose markedly from about 800,000 in 1995 to around 1.5 million in 2005. A similar but more dramatic increase was seen for visitors from the USA, climbing from roughly 500,000 to approximately 1.5 million. In contrast, Japanese tourism decreased from about 1.45 million in 1995 to just over 1.1 million in 2005.

Turning to accommodation, hotel stays increased from approximately 1.7 million in 1995 to a peak of around 2.4 million in 2000, before dropping sharply to about 1.2 million in 2005. By comparison, backpacking rose consistently throughout the period, starting at around 200,000 in 1995, increasing to roughly 700,000 in 2000, and reaching about 1.2 million in 2005, equal to hotel stays at the end of the period.

The total budget increased from £304.7 million in 2017 to £318.6 million in 2018. In both years, the national government was the primary source of funding, rising slightly from £175.5m to £177.8m. HƯỚNG DẪN VIẾT IELTS TASK 1 – PIE \+ TABLE (NATIONALITY & LOCATION)

1. Phân tích nhanh

  • Pie chart: tỷ lệ quốc tịch cư dân
  • Table: % sống ở city vs countryside

→ Dạng: composition \+ comparison

2. Introduction (paraphrase)

The pie chart shows the distribution of residents by nationality, while the table compares the percentages of each group living in cities and the countryside.

3. Overview

  • Australians chiếm đa số áp đảo
  • Các nhóm còn lại rất nhỏ
  • Tất cả quốc tịch đều chủ yếu sống ở thành phố
  • Chinese có tỷ lệ urban cao nhất

4. BODY 1 – Pie chart

Australian: 73% (dominant)

Others:

  • British: 7%
  • New Zealander: 3%
  • Chinese: 2%
  • Dutch: 1%
  • Other: 14%

→ Insight: population heavily concentrated in one group

5. BODY 2 – Table

City living (cao nhất → thấp hơn):

  • Chinese: 99% (highest)
  • New Zealander: 90%
  • British: 89%
  • Dutch: 83%
  • Australian: 80%

Countryside:

  • Australian: 20% (highest rural share)
  • Dutch: 17%
  • British: 11%
  • New Zealander: 10%
  • Chinese: 1% (lowest)

→ Insight: foreigners even more urbanized than locals

6. Từ vựng nên dùng

account for the majority

make up a small proportion

be overwhelmingly dominant

be concentrated in urban areas

have the highest/lowest proportion

by contrast

The pie chart illustrates the distribution of nationalities in Australia, while the table shows the proportions of each group living in cities and the countryside.

Overall, Australians make up by far the largest proportion of the population, and the vast majority of all nationalities live in urban areas rather than rural ones.

In terms of nationality, Australians account for 73% of the population. The next largest group is people from “other” countries at 14%. British people represent 7%, followed by New Zealanders at 3%. Chinese and Dutch populations are relatively small, at 2% and 1% respectively.

Regarding where people live, all groups are predominantly based in cities. Chinese residents are the most urbanised, with 99% living in cities and only 1% in the countryside. New Zealanders and British people also show high urban figures, at 90% and 89% respectively. Dutch residents have a slightly lower urban proportion at 83%, while Australians have the lowest city share among the groups listed, at 80%, meaning they have the highest proportion living in rural areas (20%).

guide_html:
HƯỚNG DẪN VIẾT IELTS TASK 1 – BAR CHART \+ TABLE

1. Phân tích nhanh

  • Biểu đồ cột: giá trị xuất khẩu (tỷ USD) năm 2015 vs 2016
  • Bảng: % thay đổi

→ Dạng: so sánh \+ xu hướng

2. Introduction (paraphrase)

The bar chart compares export earnings from five product categories in 2015 and 2016, while the table shows the percentage change in these values over the same period.

3. Overview (cực quan trọng)

  • Hầu hết các mặt hàng tăng
  • Textiles tăng mạnh nhất
  • Gems and jewellery là mặt hàng duy nhất giảm
  • Petroleum và engineered goods vẫn là nguồn thu lớn nhất

4. BODY 1 – So sánh số liệu chính

Petroleum:

\~60 → \~62 (cao nhất)

Engineered goods:

\~56 → \~60 (tăng đáng kể)

Gems & jewellery:

\~42 → \~40 (giảm nhẹ)

→ Nhóm top: petroleum \+ engineered

5. BODY 2 – Nhóm còn lại \+ % change

Agricultural:

\~30 → \~31 (tăng nhẹ nhất)

Textiles:

\~25 → \~31 (tăng mạnh nhất)

% change:

  • Textiles: \+15.24% (largest rise)
  • Engineered: \+8.5%
  • Petroleum: \+3%
  • Agricultural: \+0.81%
  • Gems: \-5.18% (only decline)

6. Từ vựng nên dùng

increase slightly / significantly

experience a rise

see a decline

remain the largest contributor

record the highest growth

be the only category to fall

The bar chart compares export earnings from five product categories in 2015 and 2016, while the table shows the percentage change over the same period.

Petroleum products generated the highest revenue in both years, rising slightly from about $60 billion in 2015 to roughly $62 billion in 2016. Earnings from engineered goods also increased, from approximately $56 billion to $60 billion. In contrast, gems and jewellery experienced a decline, falling from around $42 billion to $40 billion.

Agricultural products saw a marginal increase, from about $29 billion in 2015 to just over $30 billion in 2016. The most notable growth was in textiles, which rose significantly from roughly $25 billion to about $30 billion.

In terms of percentage change, textiles recorded the largest increase at 15.24%, followed by engineered goods at 8.5%. Petroleum products grew modestly by 3%, while agricultural products saw only a slight rise of 0.81%. Gems and jewellery was the only category to decrease, with a drop of 5.18%.

HƯỚNG DẪN VIẾT IELTS TASK 1 – TABLE \+ BAR CHART (MEN vs WOMEN)

1. Phân tích nhanh

  • 2 phần:
  • Table: leisure activities
  • Bar chart: household activities
  • Đơn vị: minutes per day
  • So sánh giới tính

2. Introduction (paraphrase)

The table and bar chart compare the average time spent per day by men and women in the UK on leisure and household activities in 2008.

3. Overview (rất quan trọng)

  • Men dành nhiều thời gian hơn cho leisure
  • Women dành nhiều thời gian hơn cho household
  • Biggest gap: cooking & washing
  • Smallest difference: reading

4. BODY 1 – Leisure activities

Men spend more time on entertainment:

  • TV: 137 vs 118 (largest activity overall)

Reading:

  • Nearly equal (18 vs 19)

Sport:

  • Men higher (15 vs 11)

→ Insight: men slightly dominate leisure, especially passive activities

5. BODY 2 – Household activities

Cooking & washing:

  • Women 75 vs men 30 (huge gap)

Shopping:

  • Women higher (35 vs 25)

Clothes washing:

  • Women 30 vs men 10

Repair:

  • Only category men lead (20 vs 10)

→ Insight: women do most domestic work except technical tasks

6. Từ vựng nên dùng

spend more/less time on

account for

be significantly higher than

show a similar pattern

be the only category where…

a considerable gap

The table and bar chart compare the average daily time (in minutes) spent by men and women in the UK on leisure and household activities in 2008.

Overall, men spent more time on leisure activities, particularly watching TV, while women devoted significantly more time to household tasks.

In terms of leisure, watching TV, videos and listening to the radio was the most time-consuming activity for both genders, with men spending 137 minutes per day compared to 118 minutes for women. Reading accounted for relatively little time, at 18 minutes for men and slightly higher at 19 minutes for women. Men also spent more time on sport, averaging 15 minutes daily, compared to 11 minutes for women.

Regarding household activities, women consistently spent more time than men on most tasks. Cooking and washing took up the largest share, with women spending 75 minutes per day, more than double the 30 minutes recorded for men. Similarly, women spent 35 minutes on shopping, compared to 25 minutes for men. Clothes washing and ironing also showed a notable gap, at 30 minutes for women versus only 10 minutes for men. In contrast, men spent more time on repair work, averaging 20 minutes daily, while women spent just 10 minutes on this activity.

HƯỚNG DẪN VIẾT IELTS TASK 1

1. Dạng bài

  • Mixed charts: 2 line graphs
  • Nội dung: spending \+ participation

2. Introduction (công thức)

  • two line graphs \+ spending \+ sports participation \+ children \+ time

3. Overview (ý chính, không số)

  • Spending: tăng đều theo thời gian
  • Football: luôn cao nhất
  • Athletics: tăng mạnh rồi giảm nhẹ
  • Swimming: tăng ổn định

4. Body 1 – Spending

  • tăng liên tục qua các năm
  • không có giảm

→ Key idea:

  • steady upward trend

5. Body 2 – Participation

Viết theo từng môn:

Football

  • cao nhất toàn bộ
  • tăng nhẹ

Athletics

  • tăng mạnh (đặc biệt giai đoạn giữa)
  • sau đó giảm nhẹ

Swimming

  • tăng đều
  • luôn đứng giữa

→ Key idea:

  • football dominate
  • athletics biến động mạnh nhất

6. Từ vựng cần dùng

  • increase steadily
  • rise gradually
  • peak
  • slight decline
  • remain the highest
  • fluctuate

The line graphs illustrate the average monthly expenditure on children’s sports between 2008 and 2014, along with participation levels in football, athletics and swimming over the same period.

Overall, spending on children’s sports rose steadily throughout the period. Football consistently had the highest participation, while athletics experienced the most dramatic fluctuation. Swimming showed a gradual upward trend.

Monthly spending increased from £20 in 2008 to £24 in 2010, before rising further to £28 in 2012 and reaching £32 in 2014. This indicates a continuous and moderate growth in expenditure over the six-year period.

In terms of participation, football remained the most popular sport, with the number of children rising slightly from 8.2 million in 2008 to 9.0 million in 2014, despite a minor dip in 2010. Swimming participation also grew steadily, increasing from 2.0 million to 3.8 million.

By contrast, athletics started at a relatively low level of 0.8 million in 2008 and increased marginally to 1.2 million in 2010, before surging to 5.0 million in 2012. However, this figure declined slightly to 4.5 million by 2014.

HƯỚNG DẪN VIẾT IELTS TASK 1

1. Dạng bài

  • Mixed charts: Bar chart \+ Pie chart
  • Nội dung: living alone (age \+ gender) \+ housing size

2. Introduction (công thức)

  • bar chart \+ pie chart \+ living alone \+ bedrooms \+ England \+ 2011

→ dùng: illustrate / compare / show

3. Overview (ý chính, không số)

  • Nhóm trẻ: nam cao hơn nữ
  • Nhóm lớn tuổi: nữ cao hơn nam
  • Trung niên: gần như cân bằng
  • Nhà nhỏ (1–2 phòng): chiếm đa số
  • Nhà lớn (4+ phòng): chiếm tỷ lệ rất nhỏ

4. Body 1 – Bar chart (Age \+ Gender)

Chia theo nhóm tuổi:

16–34

  • nam \> nữ

35–64

  • gần bằng nhau
  • có điểm cân bằng

65+

  • nữ \> nam
  • khoảng cách tăng theo tuổi

→ Key idea:

  • xu hướng đảo chiều theo độ tuổi

5. Body 2 – Pie chart (Bedrooms)

Theo thứ tự:

  • 2 bedrooms: lớn nhất
  • 1 và 3 bedrooms: chiếm phần lớn
  • 4 bedrooms: nhỏ
  • 5+ bedrooms: nhỏ nhất

→ Key idea:

  • nhà ít phòng chiếm ưu thế

6. Từ vựng cần dùng

  • account for
  • the majority / the minority
  • outnumber
  • be evenly distributed
  • dominate
  • make up a small proportion

The charts illustrate the proportions of males and females living alone in England in 2011 across different age groups, along with the distribution of bedroom numbers in one-person households.

Overall, younger age groups were dominated by men living alone, whereas women accounted for the majority in older age brackets. In addition, most one-person households occupied properties with either two or three bedrooms.

Among younger individuals, men were more likely to live alone. Specifically, males represented 53% of those aged 16–24 and 63% in the 25–34 group, with a peak of 65% among people aged 35–49. The gender gap then narrowed in the 50–64 group, where both sexes accounted for an equal share of 50%. Beyond this age, the pattern reversed, with women becoming increasingly dominant. Females comprised 63% of those aged 65–74, rising to 72% for the 75–84 group and peaking at 75% among individuals aged 85 and over. Overall, women made up a larger proportion of solo dwellers (56%) compared to men (44%).

Regarding housing size, two-bedroom homes were the most common among single occupants, accounting for 35.4% of cases. This was followed by three-bedroom properties at 29.8% and one-bedroom dwellings at 28.0%. Larger homes were relatively rare, with only 5.3% of individuals living in four-bedroom properties and a minimal 1.4% occupying homes with five or more bedrooms.

6. Từ khóa bắt buộc học sinh dùng

  • peak at
  • remain stable
  • decline
  • follow a similar pattern

The line graph illustrates car sales of three brands (Xbrand, Ybrand and Zbrand) from 2015 to 2019, while the pie chart shows the proportion of sales by car type.

Overall, Xbrand experienced a steady increase and became the best-selling brand by the end of the period, whereas Zbrand showed a general decline before a slight recovery. Ybrand rose initially but then fell sharply. In terms of car types, MPVs accounted for the largest share, while sedans were the least popular.

In 2015, Zbrand had the highest sales at around 3.4 million units, followed by Ybrand at approximately 1.8 million, while Xbrand recorded the lowest figure at just under 1 million. Over the next two years, Xbrand grew consistently, reaching about 1.9 million in 2017. During the same period, Ybrand increased to a peak of roughly 2.6 million, overtaking Zbrand, whose sales declined to just above 2 million.

From 2017 onwards, Xbrand continued to rise, surpassing both competitors in 2018 and reaching nearly 3 million units in 2019. In contrast, Ybrand dropped significantly after 2017, falling to around 1.6 million by the end of the period. Zbrand decreased to a low of about 1.9 million in 2018 before recovering slightly to approximately 2.3 million in 2019.

Regarding car types, MPVs made up the largest proportion at 35%, followed by SUVs at 27% and sportscars at 25%. Hatchback city cars accounted for 10%, while sedans represented only 3% of total sales.
