title: Bar Chart: The charts below show the percentage of workers in three sectors across four count...
description: The charts below show the percentage of workers in three sectors across four countries in 1980 and 2010. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features and make comparisons where relevant.
guide_html:
HƯỚNG DẪN VIẾT BÀI

IELTS Writing Task 1 – Workers in three sectors (1980 vs 2010)

TID sẽ chỉ bạn cách xử lý dạng 2 charts \+ 3 categories \+ nhiều quốc gia này sao cho không bị rối nha.

1. Hiểu đề bài

Biểu đồ cho thấy tỷ lệ lao động làm việc trong 3 ngành:

  • Agriculture
  • Industry
  • Services

ở 4 quốc gia (Germany, USA, Japan, China) vào 1980 và 2010.

TID nhắc bạn:

Dạng này cần:

  • so sánh theo thời gian
  • so sánh giữa các ngành
  • và nhận ra xu hướng chuyển dịch lao động

2. Cách viết Introduction

Paraphrase đề bài, giữ đủ:

  • tỷ lệ lao động
  • 3 ngành
  • 4 quốc gia
  • 2 năm

3. Cách viết Overview

TID gợi ý bạn các ý chính:

  • Industry trở thành ngành chiếm tỷ lệ lớn nhất ở hầu hết các nước vào 2010
  • Agriculture giảm ở tất cả các quốc gia
  • China khác biệt khi vẫn có tỷ lệ nông nghiệp cao nhất

Bạn có thể thêm:

Services có xu hướng giảm nhẹ hoặc không tăng đáng kể

4. Cách chia Body

BODY 1 – Germany, USA, Japan (nhóm tương đồng)

1980:

  • Industry chiếm tỷ lệ cao nhất (\~50–60%)
  • Services đứng thứ hai
  • Agriculture rất thấp

2010:

  • Industry tăng mạnh (Germany \~80%, Japan \~78%, USA \~70%)
  • Services giảm nhẹ
  • Agriculture tiếp tục giảm

TID gợi ý:

Bạn nên nhóm 3 nước này vì pattern rất giống nhau nha.

BODY 2 – China (khác biệt)

1980:

  • Agriculture cao nhất (\~70%)
  • Industry và Services thấp hơn

2010:

  • Agriculture giảm xuống \~50%
  • Industry giữ ở mức \~40%
  • Services giảm mạnh (\~20%)

TID lưu ý:

China vẫn là nước có tỷ lệ nông nghiệp cao nhất ở cả hai năm nha.

5. Gợi ý paraphrase

TID gợi ý bạn một số cách diễn đạt:

  • workforce / workers
  • sectors
  • accounted for / made up
  • increased / decreased significantly
  • remained dominant

Ví dụ:

Industry became the dominant sector in most countries by 2010 nha.

By contrast, agriculture declined across all four nations, although it remained the largest sector in China.

The charts compare the percentages of workers employed in agriculture, industry and services in four countries in 1980 and 2010.

Overall, industry became the dominant sector in Germany, the USA and Japan by 2010, while China continued to rely heavily on agriculture despite a decline. In most cases, the share of services decreased, whereas industry expanded significantly.

In 1980, industry already accounted for the largest proportion in Germany, the USA and Japan, at 60, 52 and 49 percent respectively. Services were the second largest sector in these countries, while agriculture remained minimal. By contrast, China had a very different structure, with 70 percent of workers in agriculture, compared to 40 percent in industry and 48 percent in services.

By 2010, industrial employment had risen sharply to 80 percent in Germany, 70 percent in the USA and 78 percent in Japan, consolidating its dominance. Meanwhile, agriculture declined slightly in these countries, remaining below 10 percent. Services, however, fell to 40 percent in Germany, 37 percent in the USA and 27 percent in Japan.

In China, agriculture dropped from 70 to 50 percent, but it still represented the largest sector. Services also decreased markedly to 20 percent, while industry remained unchanged at 40 percent.
chart_description:
TYPE: bar chart
TITLE: Percentage of workers in three sectors: 1980
UNITS/AXES: Percentage (%), 0-80 in increments of 10; Countries (Germany, USA, Japan, China); Sectors (Agriculture, Industry, Services); Years (1980, 2010)
SERIES/CATEGORIES: Germany, USA, Japan, China; Agriculture, Industry, Services
DATA:
1980:
Germany: Agriculture 4, Industry 60, Services 50
USA: Agriculture 8, Industry 52, Services 47
Japan: Agriculture 11, Industry 49, Services 39
China: Agriculture 70, Industry 40, Services 48
2010:
Germany: Agriculture 3, Industry 80, Services 40
USA: Agriculture 6, Industry 70, Services 37
Japan: Agriculture 10, Industry 78, Services 27
China: Agriculture 50, Industry 40, Services 20
KEY FEATURES:
* In 1980, China had the highest percentage of workers in agriculture (70%), while Germany had the lowest (4%).
* By 2010, Germany had the highest percentage of workers in industry (80%), and China had the highest in agriculture (50%).
* The percentage of workers in agriculture decreased in all countries from 1980 to 2010, except for Japan which remained relatively stable.
* The percentage of workers in industry increased significantly in Germany, USA, and Japan, while remaining constant in China.
* The percentage of workers in services decreased in all countries from 1980 to 2010.
* In 1980, Industry and Services were the dominant sectors in Germany, USA, and Japan, while Agriculture was dominant in China. This shifted by 2010, with Industry becoming dominant in Germany, USA, and Japan, and Agriculture still dominant in China but with a reduced percentage.

title: Bar Chart: The percentage of school-aged girls and boys who were at secondary school in four ...
description: The first chart below shows the percentage of school-aged girls and boys who were at secondary school in four regions of the world in 2000. The second chart shows the percentages of college-aged men and women in higher education in the same year. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.
guide_html:
HƯỚNG DẪN VIẾT BÀI

IELTS Writing Task 1 – Education Levels by Region

TID sẽ đi cùng bạn để xử lý dạng bar chart này một cách gọn gàng, không bị rối số liệu nha.

1. Hiểu đề bài

Biểu đồ so sánh tỷ lệ dân số đi học ở bậc trung học và bậc cao hơn giữa nam và nữ tại 4 khu vực:

  • Europe
  • Sub-Saharan Africa
  • Latin America
  • East Asia

TID nhắc bạn:

Dạng này không chỉ là “mô tả số”, mà là:

  • so sánh giữa nam và nữ
  • so sánh giữa các khu vực
  • và nhìn ra pattern chung nha

2. Cách viết Introduction

Bạn chỉ cần paraphrase đề bài thôi nha.

Giữ đủ ý:

  • tỷ lệ dân số đi học
  • hai bậc: secondary & higher education
  • nam và nữ
  • 4 khu vực

Viết gọn, không cần phân tích gì ở đây nha.

3. Cách viết Overview

TID sẽ giúp bạn chọn đúng ý quan trọng để viết nhanh phần này nha.

Bạn có thể nêu:

  • Europe có tỷ lệ đi học cao nhất ở cả hai bậc
  • Sub-Saharan Africa thấp nhất
  • Ở bậc trung học: nam và nữ khá cân bằng
  • Ở bậc đại học: nữ cao hơn nam ở Europe, nhưng thấp hơn ở các khu vực còn lại

Chỉ cần vậy là đủ rõ rồi nha, không cần số liệu.

4. Cách chia Body

BODY 1 – Secondary Education

TID gợi ý bạn đi theo từng khu vực:

  • Europe:

Gần như toàn bộ dân số đi học

Nam: 98%

Nữ: 100%

  • Sub-Saharan Africa:

Thấp nhất

Nam: 30%

Nữ: 20%

  • Latin America:

Mức trung bình

Nam: 50%

Nữ: 60%

  • East Asia:

Khá cao

Nam: 60%

Nữ: 58%

TID lưu ý:

Ở phần này bạn nên highlight là giới tính không chênh lệch nhiều nha.

BODY 2 – Higher Education
  • Europe:

Cao nhất

Nam: 60%

Nữ: 70%

  • Sub-Saharan Africa:

Rất thấp

Nam: 5%

Nữ: 2%

  • Latin America:

Nam cao hơn nữ

Nam: 20%

Nữ: 15%

  • East Asia:

Cũng thấp

Nam: 10%

Nữ: 8%

TID nhắc nhẹ:

Ở bậc này, khoảng cách giới tính rõ hơn so với secondary nha.

5. Gợi ý paraphrase

TID gợi ý bạn vài cách diễn đạt để tránh lặp từ nha:

  • percentage of people
  • proportion of the population
  • enrolment rate
  • attend / enrol in education

Ví dụ:

The chart compares the proportion of males and females attending secondary and higher education across four regions.

Overall, Europe recorded the highest participation rates, while Sub-Saharan Africa had the lowest nha.

The charts compare the proportions of males and females participating in secondary and higher education across four regions.

Overall, secondary education participation was relatively high in most regions, with smaller gender gaps, whereas higher education showed lower participation rates and more pronounced disparities. Europe consistently recorded the highest figures, while Sub Saharan Africa had by far the lowest in both categories.

In secondary education, Europe achieved near universal participation, with 98 percent of males and 100 percent of females enrolled. East Asia also reported relatively balanced figures at around 60 percent for both genders. In Latin America, female participation was higher at 60 percent compared to 50 percent for males. By contrast, Sub Saharan Africa showed a noticeable gap, with 30 percent of males attending secondary school versus only 20 percent of females.

In higher education, participation levels were considerably lower across all regions. Europe again led, with 70 percent of females and 60 percent of males enrolled. Latin America showed moderate figures, with 20 percent for males and 15 percent for females. East Asia recorded lower rates at 10 percent and 8 percent respectively. Sub Saharan Africa remained the least developed in this regard, with only 5 percent of males and 2 percent of females in higher education.
chart_description:
TYPE: bar chart
TITLE: Secondary Education; Higher Education (Colleges, Universities)
UNITS/AXES: % of school-aged population (0-120 in increments of 20); % of college-aged population (0-90 in increments of 10)
SERIES/CATEGORIES: Europe, Sub-Saharan Africa, Latin America, East Asia; Male, Female
DATA:
Secondary Education - Male: Europe 98, Sub-Saharan Africa 30, Latin America 50, East Asia 60
Secondary Education - Female: Europe 100, Sub-Saharan Africa 20, Latin America 60, East Asia 58
Higher Education - Male: Europe 60, Sub-Saharan Africa 5, Latin America 20, East Asia 10
Higher Education - Female: Europe 70, Sub-Saharan Africa 2, Latin America 15, East Asia 8
KEY FEATURES:
* In secondary education, Europe has the highest participation rates for both males and females.
* Sub-Saharan Africa has the lowest participation rates in both secondary and higher education for both genders.
* Female participation in secondary education is higher than male participation in Europe and Latin America, while male participation is slightly higher in East Asia.
* In higher education, female participation is higher than male participation in Europe, while male participation is higher in Sub-Saharan Africa, Latin America, and East Asia.
* Europe shows significantly higher participation in higher education compared to other regions for both genders.
* There is a general trend of lower participation rates in higher education compared to secondary education across all regions and genders.

title: Bar Chart: The bar charts give information about the salaries and university fees of students...
description: The bar charts give information about the salaries and university fees of students from three universities in two spheres: Law and Business. Summatise the information by selecting and reporting the main features and making comparisons where relevant.
guide_html:
HƯỚNG DẪN VIẾT BÀI

IELTS Writing Task 1 – Salaries vs Tuition Fees (Law & Business)

TID sẽ chỉ bạn cách xử lý dạng 2 charts \+ 2 variables (salary vs fees) này sao cho rõ ràng và không bị rối nha.

1. Hiểu đề bài

Biểu đồ so sánh:

  • mức lương trung bình của sinh viên sau khi tốt nghiệp
  • và học phí

ở 3 trường đại học (A, B, C), trong 2 ngành:

  • Law
  • Business

Đơn vị: nghìn đô

TID nhắc bạn:

Dạng này cần:

  • so sánh giữa salary vs tuition
  • so sánh giữa các trường
  • và so sánh giữa 2 ngành

2. Cách viết Introduction

Paraphrase đề bài, giữ đủ:

  • lương và học phí
  • 2 ngành
  • 3 trường
  • đơn vị

3. Cách viết Overview

TID gợi ý bạn các ý chính:

  • Học phí luôn cao hơn lương ở hầu hết các trường
  • University C có mức học phí cao nhất trong cả hai ngành
  • Salary trong ngành Law khá ổn định, trong khi Business có sự chênh lệch rõ hơn

Bạn cũng có thể thêm:

Law có mức lương cao hơn Business ở một số trường

4. Cách chia Body

BODY 1 – Law
  • University A:

Salary \= 40

Fees \= 40

  • University B:

Salary \= 40

Fees \= 60

  • University C:

Salary \= 37

Fees \= 55

TID lưu ý:

Fees luôn cao hơn salary (trừ A), và B là cao nhất nha.

BODY 2 – Business
  • University A:

Salary \= 30

Fees \= 45

  • University B:

Salary \= 40

Fees \= 50

  • University C:

Salary \= 40

Fees \= 60

TID gợi ý:

Bạn có thể highlight:

  • Salary tăng từ A → C
  • Fees cũng tăng rõ theo cùng xu hướng

5. Gợi ý paraphrase

TID gợi ý bạn một số cách diễn đạt:

  • average salary / tuition fees
  • figures / amounts
  • higher than / lower than
  • increased / remained stable

Ví dụ:

Tuition fees were generally higher than the average salaries across most universities nha.

University C recorded the highest fees in both subjects.

The charts compare average salaries of graduates and tuition fees for law and business students at three universities, measured in thousands of dollars.

Overall, tuition fees were consistently higher than salaries across most cases, particularly in business courses. University C generally recorded the highest fees, while salaries varied less noticeably between institutions.

For law, University A showed equal figures for salary and tuition at 40 thousand dollars. In contrast, University B had a significant gap, with salaries at 40 compared to fees of 60. A similar pattern is seen at University C, where graduates earned 37 while paying 55 in fees.

In business, salaries were lower at University A at 30, while fees stood at 45. At University B, salaries increased to 40, with fees rising to 50. University C again recorded the highest figures, with salaries at 40 and tuition reaching 60, indicating the widest disparity among the three institutions.
chart_description:
TYPE: bar chart
TITLE: Average salaries of university students and their tuition fees in thousands of dollars
UNITS/AXES: Y-axis: Thousands of dollars, X-axis: University A, University B, University C
SERIES/CATEGORIES: Law - Salary, Law - Tuition fees, Business - Salary, Business - Tuition fees
DATA:
Law - Salary: University A: 40, University B: 40, University C: 37
Law - Tuition fees: University A: 40, University B: 60, University C: 55
Business - Salary: University A: 30, University B: 40, University C: 40
Business - Tuition fees: University A: 45, University B: 50, University C: 60
KEY FEATURES:
* For Law students, tuition fees are generally higher than salaries, except at University A where they are equal.
* University B has the highest tuition fees for both Law and Business students, at 60 thousand dollars.
* University C has the lowest salary for Law students (37 thousand dollars).
* Business students at University A have the lowest salary (30 thousand dollars).
* Tuition fees for Business students consistently increase from University A to University C.
* Salaries for Business students are lower than tuition fees across all three universities.

title: Bar Chart: Information about the actual and expected figures of population of three cities, J...
description: The chart shows information about the actual and expected figures of population of three cities, Jakarta, Sao Paulo, and Shanghai. Summarize the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.
guide_html:
HƯỚNG DẪN VIẾT BÀI

IELTS Writing Task 1 – Population size (1990 vs 2000)

TID sẽ chỉ bạn cách xử lý dạng bar chart có prediction vs actual này sao cho rõ ý, không bị rối nha.

1. Hiểu đề bài

Biểu đồ cho thấy dân số (triệu người) của 3 thành phố:

  • Jakarta
  • Shanghai
  • Sao Paulo

vào năm 1990, cùng với dự đoán năm 2000 và số liệu thực tế năm 2000.

TID nhắc bạn:

Dạng này có 3 lớp thông tin, nên bạn cần:

  • so sánh theo thời gian (1990 → 2000)
  • so sánh giữa dự đoán và thực tế

2. Cách viết Introduction

Paraphrase đề bài, giữ đủ:

  • dân số
  • 3 thành phố
  • 1990, 2000 (prediction & actual)

Viết gọn là được nha.

3. Cách viết Overview

TID gợi ý các ý chính:

  • Dân số tăng ở tất cả các thành phố
  • Sao Paulo luôn có dân số lớn nhất, Jakarta nhỏ nhất
  • Số liệu thực tế năm 2000 đều cao hơn dự đoán

Chỉ cần 2–3 câu vậy là đủ overview nha.

4. Cách chia Body

BODY 1 – Sao Paulo (nổi bật nhất)
  • 1990: khoảng 18 triệu
  • Dự đoán 2000: \~22 triệu
  • Thực tế 2000: \~24 triệu

TID gợi ý:

Bạn nên nhấn mạnh đây là thành phố đông dân nhất và tăng mạnh nha.

BODY 2 – Shanghai & Jakarta
  • Shanghai:

1990: \~12 triệu

Dự đoán: \~14 triệu

Thực tế: \~16 triệu

  • Jakarta:

1990: \~8 triệu

Dự đoán: \~11 triệu

Thực tế: \~13 triệu

TID lưu ý:

Cả hai thành phố đều:

  • tăng đều
  • và số thực tế đều cao hơn dự đoán

5. Gợi ý paraphrase

TID gợi ý bạn một số cách diễn đạt:

  • population / population size
  • was projected to / was expected to
  • actual figures / recorded figures
  • increased / grew steadily

Ví dụ:

The population of all three cities increased over the period, with actual figures exceeding predictions in 2000 nha.

Sao Paulo remained the largest city, experiencing the most significant growth.

The chart compares the population sizes of Jakarta, Shanghai and Sao Paulo in 1990, alongside predicted and actual figures for 2000, measured in millions.

Overall, all three cities experienced population growth over the period. Sao Paulo remained by far the largest city, while Jakarta had the smallest population. In each case, the actual figures in 2000 slightly exceeded the earlier predictions.

In 1990, Sao Paulo had the highest population at around 18 million, followed by Shanghai at approximately 12 million and Jakarta at about 9 million. By 2000, all cities were expected to grow, with projections of roughly 22 million for Sao Paulo, 14 million for Shanghai and 11 million for Jakarta.

However, the actual figures in 2000 were marginally higher than predicted. Sao Paulo reached about 24 million, while Shanghai rose to around 16 million. Jakarta also increased to approximately 13 million, maintaining its position as the smallest of the three cities despite steady growth.
chart_description:
TYPE: bar chart
TITLE: Population size (1990-2000)
UNITS/AXES: X-axis: In millions, from 0 to 25 in increments of 5. Y-axis: Cities (Jakarta, Shanghai, Sao Paulo). Time span: 1990-2000.
SERIES/CATEGORIES: Cities: Jakarta, Shanghai, Sao Paulo. Data types: 1990, 2000 in prediction, 2000 actual figures.
DATA:
Jakarta:
  1990: ≈8.5 million
  2000 in prediction: ≈12.5 million
  2000 actual figures: ≈1.5 million (added to prediction, total ≈14 million)
Shanghai:
  1990: ≈13 million
  2000 in prediction: ≈15 million
  2000 actual figures: ≈2 million (added to prediction, total ≈17 million)
Sao Paulo:
  1990: ≈18 million
  2000 in prediction: ≈22 million
  2000 actual figures: ≈2 million (added to prediction, total ≈24 million)
KEY FEATURES:
* Sao Paulo had the largest population in 1990 and the largest predicted and actual population in 2000.
* Jakarta had the smallest population in 1990 and the smallest predicted and actual population in 2000.
* For all three cities, the actual population in 2000 exceeded the predicted population for 2000.
* The increase from 1990 to the actual 2000 figures was largest for Sao Paulo.
* The difference between the predicted and actual figures for 2000 was similar for Shanghai and Sao Paulo (both around 2 million).

title: Bar Chart: The charts below give information on the ages of people when they got married in o...
description: The charts below give information on the ages of people when they got married in one particular country in 1998 and 2008.
guide_html:
HƯỚNG DẪN VIẾT BÀI

IELTS Writing Task 1 – Age when getting married (1998 vs 2008)

TID sẽ chỉ bạn cách xử lý dạng 2 charts \+ nhiều nhóm tuổi sao cho gọn, dễ nhìn ra xu hướng nha.

1. Hiểu đề bài

Biểu đồ cho thấy tỷ lệ nam và nữ kết hôn ở các nhóm tuổi khác nhau vào 1998 và 2008.

TID nhắc bạn:

Đây là dạng comparison \+ time, nên bạn cần:

  • so sánh nam và nữ
  • so sánh giữa các nhóm tuổi
  • và so sánh giữa 2 năm

Không cần viết tất cả số liệu, chỉ chọn điểm nổi bật thôi nha.

2. Cách viết Introduction

Paraphrase đề bài, giữ đủ:

  • độ tuổi kết hôn
  • nam và nữ
  • các nhóm tuổi
  • 2 năm

Viết gọn là được nha.

3. Cách viết Overview

TID gợi ý bạn các ý chính:

  • Độ tuổi kết hôn có xu hướng dịch chuyển sang nhóm tuổi cao hơn vào 2008
  • Ở 1998: nữ kết hôn sớm hơn nam
  • Ở 2008: nam lại có xu hướng kết hôn muộn hơn và chiếm tỷ lệ cao hơn ở các nhóm tuổi lớn

Chỉ cần 2–3 câu như vậy là đủ overview nha.

4. Cách chia Body

BODY 1 – Năm 1998
  • Nữ:

Tập trung nhiều nhất ở nhóm 25–29 (\~11%)

Sau đó giảm dần ở các nhóm tuổi lớn hơn

  • Nam:

Cao nhất ở 25–29 và 30–34 (\~9%)

Xu hướng kết hôn muộn hơn nữ (cao hơn ở các nhóm tuổi lớn như 35–39, 40–44)

  • Nhóm trẻ (16–19):

Rất thấp ở cả hai giới

TID lưu ý:

1998 \= nữ kết hôn sớm hơn nam nha.

BODY 2 – Năm 2008
  • Nữ:

Vẫn cao nhất ở 25–29 (\~11%)

Nhưng giảm mạnh ở nhóm trẻ (20–24, 16–19)

  • Nam:

Cao nhất ở 30–34 (\~11%)

Tăng rõ ở các nhóm tuổi lớn (35–39, 40–44)

  • So sánh chung:

Nam vượt nữ ở các nhóm tuổi lớn

→ cho thấy xu hướng kết hôn muộn hơn

5. Gợi ý paraphrase

TID gợi ý bạn một số cách diễn đạt:

  • age group
  • proportion / percentage
  • get married / marry
  • peak at / be highest at
  • shift towards older age groups

Ví dụ:

The proportion of people getting married shifted towards older age groups in 2008 nha.

Men tended to marry later than women, particularly in the older age brackets.

The charts compare the percentages of males and females getting married across different age groups in 1998 and 2008.

Overall, the age at marriage shifted towards older groups over the decade. In 1998, most marriages occurred in the 25–29 age group for both genders, whereas by 2008 the peak moved to 30–34, particularly for men. Additionally, early marriages became less common, especially among females.

In 1998, females were more likely to marry at younger ages, with around 6 percent in the 20–24 group compared to roughly 2.5 percent of males. The highest figures were recorded in the 25–29 group, at about 11 percent for females and 9 percent for males. Beyond this, male participation exceeded that of females in older groups such as 30–34 and 35–39.

By 2008, participation in younger age groups declined notably. The proportion of females marrying at 20–24 fell to around 3 percent, while the figure for males dropped to about 1.5 percent. In contrast, marriage rates increased in older groups. The 30–34 category became the most common for males at approximately 11 percent, while females still peaked at 25–29, although the gap with 30–34 narrowed. Substantial increases were also seen in the 35–39 and 40–44 groups, particularly among men.

title: Bar Chart: The average prices per kilometre of clothing imported into the European Union from...
description: The average prices per kilometre of clothing imported into the European Union from six different countries in 1993 and 2003 are shown in the bar chart below. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.
guide_html:
HƯỚNG DẪN VIẾT BÀI

IELTS Writing Task 1 – Clothing prices across countries

TID sẽ chỉ bạn cách xử lý dạng bar chart so sánh 2 năm \+ nhiều quốc gia này sao cho gọn và rõ nha.

1. Hiểu đề bài

Biểu đồ cho thấy giá trung bình quần áo (bảng Anh) ở 6 quốc gia vào năm 1993 và 2003:

  • Argentina
  • Brazil
  • Japan
  • China
  • India
  • Bangladesh

TID nhắc bạn:

Dạng này cần:

  • so sánh theo thời gian
  • so sánh giữa các quốc gia
  • tìm xu hướng tăng/giảm

2. Cách viết Introduction

Paraphrase đề bài, giữ đủ:

  • giá quần áo
  • các quốc gia
  • 2 năm
  • đơn vị

3. Cách viết Overview

TID gợi ý version “ăn điểm”:

  • Giá giảm ở Argentina và Japan, giữ nguyên ở Brazil
  • Tăng rõ ở China, India và Bangladesh
  • Argentina vẫn là nước có giá cao nhất, trong khi Bangladesh thấp nhất

4. Cách chia Body

BODY 1 – Nhóm giá cao (Argentina, Brazil, Japan)
  • Argentina:

28 → 26 (giảm nhẹ, vẫn cao nhất)

  • Brazil:

23 → 23 (không đổi)

  • Japan:

15 → 13 (giảm)

TID chốt:

Nhóm này có xu hướng giảm hoặc ổn định nha.

BODY 2 – Nhóm giá thấp (China, India, Bangladesh)
  • China:

10 → 17 (tăng mạnh)

  • India:

7 → 12 (tăng)

  • Bangladesh:

3 → 6 (tăng)

TID chốt:

Nhóm này đều tăng rõ, đặc biệt China nha.

5. Gợi ý paraphrase

  • average price
  • remained stable
  • increased significantly
  • highest / lowest

Ví dụ:

Prices in Argentina remained the highest despite a slight decline nha.

By contrast, countries such as China and India saw noticeable increases over the period.

The bar chart compares the average price of clothing per kilometre in six countries in 1993 and 2003, measured in pounds.

Overall, prices declined in the higher-cost countries such as Argentina and Japan, while they increased in lower-cost markets including China, India and Bangladesh. Brazil remained unchanged over the period.

In 1993, Argentina had the highest price at £28, followed by Brazil at £23 and Japan at £15. By 2003, prices in Argentina fell slightly to £26, while Japan decreased to £13. Brazil showed no change, remaining at £23 in both years.

In contrast, notable increases occurred in developing countries. China rose significantly from £10 to £17, becoming one of the higher-priced markets by 2003. India also increased from £7 to £12, while Bangladesh doubled from £3 to £6, although it still remained the cheapest overall.
chart_description:
TYPE: bar chart
TITLE: The average price per kilometre clothing
UNITS/AXES: Y-axis: Price in pounds (£), scale 0 to 30 in increments of 5. X-axis: Countries (Argentina, Brazil, Japan, China, India, Bangladesh).
SERIES/CATEGORIES: 1993 (pink bars), 2003 (blue bars)
DATA:
Argentina: 1993: 28, 2003: 26
Brazil: 1993: 23, 2003: 23
Japan: 1993: 15, 2003: 13
China: 1993: 10, 2003: 17
India: 1993: 7, 2003: 12
Bangladesh: 1993: 3, 2003: 6
KEY FEATURES:
* Argentina had the highest average price in 1993 (£28) and 2003 (£26).
* Bangladesh had the lowest average price in both 1993 (£3) and 2003 (£6).
* The price decreased in Argentina and Japan between 1993 and 2003.
* The price remained constant in Brazil between 1993 and 2003.
* The price increased in China, India, and Bangladesh between 1993 and 2003.
* China experienced the largest increase in price, from £10 in 1993 to £17 in 2003.

title: Bar Chart: The spending (in dollars) per household in the US on five different products in 20...
description: The chart below shows the spending (in dollars) per household in the US on five different products in 2010 and 2014. Summarize the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.
guide_html:
HƯỚNG DẪN VIẾT BÀI

IELTS Writing Task 1 – Consumer spending (2010 vs 2014)

TID sẽ chỉ bạn cách xử lý dạng bar chart so sánh chi tiêu theo danh mục \+ 2 năm sao cho rõ ý và dễ viết nha.

1. Hiểu đề bài

Biểu đồ cho thấy mức chi tiêu (triệu đô) cho 5 mặt hàng:

  • Food
  • Clothes
  • Books
  • Smartphones
  • Toiletries

trong hai năm: 2010 và 2014.

TID nhắc bạn:

Dạng này cần:

  • so sánh giữa các categories
  • nhận diện tăng/giảm

2. Cách viết Introduction

Paraphrase đề, giữ đủ:

  • spending
  • categories
  • 2 năm
  • đơn vị

3. Cách viết Overview

TID gợi ý overview:

  • Chi tiêu tăng ở hầu hết các mặt hàng, ngoại trừ books
  • Food vẫn là hạng mục chi tiêu cao nhất
  • Smartphones ghi nhận mức tăng đáng kể nhất

4. Cách chia Body

BODY 1 – Nhóm chi tiêu cao (Food, Clothes)
  • Food:

3700 → 4400 (tăng mạnh, cao nhất)

  • Clothes:

2500 → 2500 (không đổi)

TID chốt:

→ nhóm này luôn chiếm phần lớn ngân sách nha

BODY 2 – Nhóm còn lại (Books, Smartphones, Toiletries)
  • Books:

1000 → 500 (giảm mạnh)

  • Smartphones:

2000 → 2700 (tăng mạnh nhất)

  • Toiletries:

1900 → 2000 (tăng nhẹ)

TID chốt:

→ xu hướng trái ngược: books giảm, smartphones tăng mạnh

5. Gợi ý paraphrase

  • consumer spending
  • expenditure on
  • remained unchanged
  • increased significantly
  • saw a sharp decline

Ví dụ:

Spending on food increased significantly and remained the highest category nha.

In contrast, expenditure on books saw a sharp decline over the period.

The bar chart compares consumer spending on five categories in 2010 and 2014, measured in millions of dollars.

Overall, food remained the largest expenditure in both years, while books accounted for the smallest share and declined further. Most categories experienced growth over the period, with smartphones showing the most notable increase, whereas spending on books fell significantly and clothing remained unchanged.

In 2010, food dominated at 3,700 million dollars, rising to 4,400 million in 2014. Smartphone spending also increased sharply from 2,000 to 2,700 million, becoming the second largest category. Toiletries saw only a slight rise from 1,900 to 2,000 million.

By contrast, clothing expenditure stayed constant at 2,500 million in both years. Books, however, declined markedly from 1,000 to just 500 million, making it the only category to experience a substantial drop.

TYPE: bar chart
TITLE: none
UNITS/AXES: Y-axis: $ million, X-axis: Food, Clothes, Books, Smartphones, Toiletries
SERIES/CATEGORIES: 2010, 2014
DATA:

Clothes: 2010: 2,500; 2014: 2,500
Books: 2010: 1,000; 2014: 500
Smartphones: 2010: 2,000; 2014: 2,700

* Food had the highest spending in both years, increasing from $3,700 million to $4,400 million.
* Books saw the largest decrease in spending, falling from $1,000 million in 2010 to $500 million in 2014.
* Spending on Clothes remained constant at $2,500 million in both years.
* Smartphones experienced a significant increase in spending, from $2,000 million to $2,700 million.
* Toiletries showed a slight increase in spending, from $1,900 million to $2,000 million.

title: Bar Chart: Information about fuel used in the transport sector in different countries in Europ...
description: The chart below shows information about fuel used in the transport sector in diï¬€erent countries in Europe, compared to the EU average, in 2009 and 2010. Summarize the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.
guide_html:
HƯỚNG DẪN VIẾT BÀI

IELTS Writing Task 1 – Fuel Use in Transport (EU Countries)

TID sẽ chỉ bạn cách xử lý dạng bar chart so sánh 2 năm này sao cho rõ ý, không bị rối số liệu nha.

1. Hiểu đề bài

Biểu đồ so sánh tỷ lệ nhiên liệu được sử dụng trong lĩnh vực giao thông ở 6 quốc gia châu Âu, kèm theo mức trung bình của EU, vào 2 năm: 2009 và 2010.

TID nhắc bạn:

Dạng này là comparison between two years, nên bạn cần:

  • so sánh giữa các quốc gia
  • và so sánh sự thay đổi giữa 2009 và 2010

Không cần viết hết số, chỉ chọn số tiêu biểu thôi nha.

2. Cách viết Introduction

Bạn chỉ cần paraphrase đề bài thôi nha.

Giữ đủ:

  • tỷ lệ nhiên liệu sử dụng
  • lĩnh vực giao thông
  • các quốc gia \+ EU average
  • 2 năm

3. Cách viết Overview

TID gợi ý bạn 2 ý chính:

  • Slovakia có tỷ lệ cao nhất, trong khi Greece thấp nhất ở cả hai năm
  • Một số nước tăng nhẹ (Italy, France, Greece), trong khi các nước khác giảm (Slovakia, Spain, EU average), và Austria giữ nguyên

Chỉ cần vậy là đủ overview rồi nha.

4. Cách chia Body

BODY 1 – Nhóm cao và nổi bật
  • Slovakia:

Cao nhất ở cả hai năm

Giảm từ 8.8% xuống 6.5%

  • Austria:

Ổn định

Giữ nguyên ở mức 5.2%

  • EU Average:

Khá cao

Giảm nhẹ từ 6.0% xuống 5.0%

TID gợi ý: nhóm này bạn nên nhấn mạnh mức cao và sự ổn định/giảm nhẹ nha.

BODY 2 – Nhóm còn lại
  • Italy:

Tăng nhẹ

4.5% → 5.2%

  • France:

Tăng nhẹ

3.7% → 4.3%

  • Spain:

Giảm

3.8% → 3.0%

  • Greece:

Thấp nhất nhưng tăng

1.2% → 2.0%

TID lưu ý:

Bạn có thể highlight Greece là nước thấp nhất nhưng tăng rõ nha.

5. Gợi ý paraphrase

TID gợi ý bạn một số cách diễn đạt:

  • percentage / proportion
  • fuel consumption / fuel use
  • increased / decreased / remained stable
  • slightly / significantly

Ví dụ:

Slovakia recorded the highest proportion of fuel use in transport, although this figure declined noticeably in 2010.

By contrast, Greece remained the lowest despite a moderate increase nha.

\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_

The bar chart compares the percentage of fuel used in the transport sector across six EU countries in 2009 and 2010, alongside the overall EU average.

Overall, Slovakia recorded the highest proportions in both years, despite a noticeable decline, while Greece had the lowest figures, although it experienced an increase. In general, changes between the two years were relatively modest, with a mix of slight rises and falls across countries.

In 2009, Slovakia led by a clear margin at 8.8 percent, followed by the EU average at 6.0 percent. Austria and Italy recorded similar levels at around 5.2 and 4.5 percent respectively, while France and Spain stood slightly lower at 3.7 and 3.8 percent. Greece had by far the smallest share at just 1.2 percent. By 2010, Slovakia’s figure had dropped significantly to 6.5 percent, although it remained the highest. Spain also saw a decline to 3.0 percent.

In contrast, several countries experienced increases. Italy rose from 4.5 to 5.2 percent, while France grew from 3.7 to 4.3 percent. Greece also increased notably to 2.0 percent, although it still ranked last. Austria remained unchanged at 5.2 percent, and the EU average decreased slightly from 6.0 to 5.0 percent.
chart_description:
TYPE: bar chart
TITLE: The percentage of fuel used in transport sector in 6 EU countries, compared to the average
UNITS/AXES: Y-axis: Percentage of fuel used (%), X-axis: Countries (Slovakia, Italy, France, Austria, Spain, Greece) and EU Average, Years: 2009, 2010
SERIES/CATEGORIES: 2009, 2010, Slovakia, Italy, France, Austria, Spain, Greece, EU Average
DATA:
2009: Slovakia 8.8, Italy 4.5, France 3.7, Austria 5.2, Spain 3.8, Greece 1.2, EU Average 6.0
2010: Slovakia 6.5, Italy 5.2, France 4.3, Austria 5.2, Spain 3.0, Greece 2.0, EU Average 5.0
KEY FEATURES:
* Slovakia had the highest percentage of fuel used in 2009 (8.8%) and 2010 (6.5%) among the listed countries.
* Greece consistently had the lowest percentage of fuel used in both years (1.2% in 2009 and 2.0% in 2010).
* The EU average decreased from 6.0% in 2009 to 5.0% in 2010.
* Most countries showed a decrease in fuel usage from 2009 to 2010, with the exception of Italy and Greece, which saw an increase, and Austria, which remained constant.
* Austria's fuel usage remained the same at 5.2% in both 2009 and 2010.

title: Bar Chart: Different methods of waste disposal in a European country from 2005 to 2008
description: The chart below shows different methods of waste disposal in a European country from 2005 to 2008. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.
guide_html:
HƯỚNG DẪN VIẾT BÀI

IELTS Writing Task 1 – Waste Disposal Methods

TID sẽ chỉ bạn cách xử lý dạng bar chart theo thời gian này sao cho mạch lạc, dễ viết và không bị kể số liệu nha.

1. Hiểu đề bài

Biểu đồ cho thấy lượng rác (triệu tấn) được xử lý bằng 3 phương pháp:

  • chôn lấp (landfill)
  • đốt (burning)
  • đổ ra biển (dumping in sea)

qua 4 năm: 2005, 2006, 2007 và 2008.

TID nhắc bạn:

Đây là dạng time \+ multiple categories, nên bạn cần:

  • theo dõi xu hướng của từng phương pháp
  • so sánh giữa các phương pháp theo từng năm

2. Cách viết Introduction

Bạn chỉ cần paraphrase đề bài thôi nha.

Giữ đủ:

  • lượng rác
  • phương pháp xử lý
  • đơn vị (million tonnes)
  • các năm

3. Cách viết Overview

TID gợi ý bạn 2–3 ý chính:

  • Landfill giảm đều theo thời gian
  • Burning biến động nhưng kết thúc ở mức cao
  • Dumping in sea nhìn chung giảm hoặc dao động nhẹ

Bạn cũng có thể thêm:

  • Landfill là phương pháp cao nhất ở đầu kỳ, nhưng không còn dẫn đầu ở cuối kỳ

4. Cách chia Body

BODY 1 – Landfill & Dumping (xu hướng giảm)
  • Landfill:

Giảm liên tục

70 → 60 → 50 → 40

  • Dumping in sea:

Giảm nhẹ tổng thể

55 → 50 → 50 → 40

TID gợi ý:

Bạn có thể so sánh 2 phương pháp này vì đều đi xuống nha.

BODY 2 – Burning (xu hướng khác biệt)
  • Burning:

Giảm nhẹ rồi tăng mạnh

65 → 60 → 40 → 65

TID lưu ý:

Đây là phương pháp dao động rõ nhất, nên tách riêng để viết sẽ rõ hơn nha.

Bạn cũng có thể thêm:

Nó trở thành cao nhất vào năm 2008.

5. Gợi ý paraphrase

TID gợi ý bạn vài cách diễn đạt:

  • amount / volume of waste
  • disposal methods
  • increased / decreased / fluctuated
  • reached a peak / fell to

Ví dụ:

The amount of waste disposed of by landfill decreased steadily over the period nha.

By contrast, burning fluctuated significantly before rising again in the final year.

The bar chart compares the amount of waste disposed of by three methods between 2005 and 2008, measured in million tonnes.

Overall, landfill use declined steadily over the period, while burning fluctuated but ended as the dominant method. Dumping in the sea showed a slight overall decrease, despite a temporary rise in 2007.

In 2005, landfill was the primary method at 70 million tonnes, followed by burning at 65 and sea dumping at 55. By 2006, landfill had fallen to 60, equalling burning, while sea dumping dropped to 50. The downward trend in landfill continued in 2007, reaching 50, whereas burning decreased further to 40. In contrast, sea dumping rebounded to 50, matching landfill.

By 2008, landfill declined to its lowest point at 40 million tonnes. Burning, however, rose sharply to 65, becoming the most widely used method. Sea dumping returned to 40, the same level as landfill, indicating a convergence of these two methods at the end of the period.
chart_description:
TYPE: bar chart
TITLE: Amount of waste by method of disposal (in million tonnes)
UNITS/AXES: Y-axis: Amount in million tonnes, scale 0-80 in increments of 10. X-axis: Years 2005, 2006, 2007, 2008.
SERIES/CATEGORIES: Landfill, Burning, Dumping in sea
DATA:
Landfill: 2005: 70, 2006: 60, 2007: 50, 2008: 40
Burning: 2005: 65, 2006: 60, 2007: 40, 2008: 65
Dumping in sea: 2005: 55, 2006: 50, 2007: 50, 2008: 40
KEY FEATURES:
* Landfill waste consistently decreased over the period.
* Burning waste fluctuated, starting and ending at the same level.
* Dumping in sea waste generally decreased, with a stable period in the middle.
* In 2005, Landfill was the highest method of disposal.
* In 2008, Burning was the highest method of disposal.
* The lowest amount of waste disposal for any method was 40 million tonnes, occurring multiple times.

title: Bar Chart: The percentage of the population in the UK who consumed the recommended daily amou...

HƯỚNG DẪN VIẾT BÀI

IELTS Writing Task 1 – Fruit & Vegetable Intake in the UK

TID sẽ chỉ bạn cách xử lý dạng bar chart theo thời gian này sao cho rõ ràng, dễ viết và không bị lan man nha.

1. Hiểu đề bài

Biểu đồ cho thấy tỷ lệ người ở Anh ăn đủ trái cây và rau theo khuyến nghị, chia theo 3 nhóm:

  • Men
  • Women
  • Children

qua 3 năm: 2002, 2006 và 2010.

TID nhắc bạn:

Dạng này là time \+ group comparison, nên bạn cần:

  • so sánh giữa các nhóm
  • theo dõi sự thay đổi theo thời gian

2. Cách viết Introduction

Bạn chỉ cần paraphrase đề bài thôi nha.

Giữ đủ:

  • tỷ lệ tiêu thụ trái cây và rau
  • 3 nhóm đối tượng
  • 3 mốc thời gian

3. Cách viết Overview

TID gợi ý bạn các ý chính:

  • Women luôn có tỷ lệ cao nhất, trong khi Children thấp nhất
  • Tất cả các nhóm đều tăng từ 2002 đến 2006, sau đó giảm nhẹ vào 2010
  • 2006 là năm đạt đỉnh cho cả ba nhóm

Chỉ cần 2–3 câu như vậy là đủ nha.

4. Cách chia Body

BODY 1 – Women & Men
  • Women:

Luôn cao nhất

24.5 → 32 → 27

  • Men:

Thấp hơn women nhưng cùng xu hướng

22 → 28 → 24

TID gợi ý:

Bạn nên highlight là hai nhóm này có xu hướng giống nhau nha.

BODY 2 – Children
  • Children:

Luôn thấp nhất

11 → 16 → 13.5

  • Xu hướng:

Tăng đến 2006 rồi giảm

TID lưu ý:

Bạn có thể thêm là khoảng cách giữa children và adults vẫn khá lớn nha.

5. Gợi ý paraphrase

TID gợi ý bạn một số cách diễn đạt:

  • proportion / percentage
  • consume / intake
  • meet the recommended amount
  • peaked at / declined slightly

Ví dụ:

The proportion of women meeting the recommended intake was consistently the highest across the period nha.

All groups peaked in 2006 before experiencing a slight decline in 2010.

The bar chart compares the proportions of men, women and children in the UK who consumed fruit and vegetables in 2002, 2006 and 2010.

Overall, women consistently recorded the highest intake, while children had the lowest figures throughout. All three groups saw an increase from 2002 to 2006, followed by a slight decline in 2010, although levels remained above those at the beginning of the period.

In 2002, 24.5 percent of women met the intake level, compared to 22 percent of men and only 11 percent of children. By 2006, consumption rose across all groups, reaching a peak of 32 percent for women, 28 percent for men and 16 percent for children.

However, in 2010, the proportions fell moderately. Women declined to 27 percent and men to 24 percent, while children dropped to 13.5 percent. Despite this decrease, each group maintained higher levels than in 2002, indicating an overall improvement over the period.

* Women consistently had the highest percentage of fruit and vegetable intake across all three years.
* Children consistently had the lowest percentage of fruit and vegetable intake across all three years.

guide_html:
HƯỚNG DẪN VIẾT BÀI

IELTS Writing Task 1 – Working hours across countries

TID sẽ chỉ bạn cách xử lý dạng 4 charts \+ cùng 1 biến (working hours) này sao cho gọn, không bị kể lan man nha.

1. Hiểu đề bài

Biểu đồ cho thấy tỷ lệ người lao động làm việc theo các khoảng giờ khác nhau (từ 1–14 đến 50+) ở 4 quốc gia:

  • France
  • Denmark
  • Sweden
  • The UK

TID nhắc bạn:

Dạng này cần:

  • so sánh giữa các quốc gia
  • tìm nhóm giờ phổ biến nhất
  • nhận ra pattern chung

2. Cách viết Introduction

Paraphrase đề bài, giữ đủ:

  • tỷ lệ lao động
  • số giờ làm việc
  • 4 quốc gia

Viết gọn là được nha.

3. Cách viết Overview

TID gợi ý bạn các ý chính:

  • Nhóm giờ 36–40 là phổ biến nhất ở hầu hết các quốc gia
  • Sweden có tỷ lệ cao nhất ở nhóm này
  • UK có xu hướng làm việc nhiều giờ hơn (tỷ lệ cao ở nhóm 46–50 và 50+)
  • France và Denmark có phân bố cân bằng hơn

Chỉ cần 2–3 câu vậy là đủ nha.

4. Cách chia Body

BODY 1 – France & Denmark
  • France:

Cao nhất ở 31–35 (\~50%) và 36–40 (\~36%)

Các nhóm còn lại thấp hơn đáng kể

  • Denmark:

Đỉnh ở 36–40 (\~70%)

Các nhóm khác khá thấp và phân bố đều

TID lưu ý:

Denmark có peak rất rõ ở 36–40 nha.

BODY 2 – Sweden & UK
  • Sweden:

Cao nhất ở 36–40 (\~80%)

Sau đó giảm mạnh ở các nhóm giờ cao hơn

  • UK:

36–40 cao (\~48%)

Nhưng các nhóm giờ cao (41–45, 46–50, 50+) vẫn khá lớn

TID gợi ý:

Bạn nên highlight UK là nước có xu hướng làm việc nhiều giờ hơn nha.

5. Gợi ý paraphrase

TID gợi ý bạn một số cách diễn đạt:

  • working hours
  • proportion of workers
  • peaked at / was highest at
  • distribution / pattern
  • long working hours

Ví dụ:

The proportion of workers peaked at 36–40 hours in most countries nha.

The UK had a higher proportion of people working longer hours compared to the other countries.

The charts compare the distribution of working hours among employees in France, Denmark, Sweden and the UK.

Overall, mid-range working hours accounted for the largest proportions in most countries, although the dominant category differed. Sweden and Denmark were heavily concentrated in the 36–40 hour group, while France peaked slightly earlier at 31–35 hours. The UK showed a more even spread, with a notable share of employees working longer hours.

In France, the highest proportion of workers fell in the 31–35 hour range at 50 percent, followed by 36–40 hours at 36 percent. Other categories were considerably lower, with relatively small shares at both the shortest and longest working hours.

Denmark displayed a strong concentration in the 36–40 hour group, which accounted for 70 percent of workers. The next largest category was 31–35 hours at 22 percent, while all other ranges remained below 15 percent.

A similar but more pronounced pattern is observed in Sweden, where 80 percent of employees worked 36–40 hours, the highest figure across all countries. The 31–35 and 41–45 categories followed at 35 and 28 percent respectively.

In contrast, the UK showed a broader distribution. Although 36–40 hours was still the largest category at 48 percent, a relatively high proportion of workers were in longer-hour groups, including 18 percent in 46–50 hours and 21 percent in the 50+ category, indicating a greater tendency toward extended working hours.

title: Bar Chart: The graphs below show the total percentage of films released and the total percent...

guide_html:
IELTS Writing Task 1 –

Films released & cinema ticket sales (1996 vs 2000\)

TID sẽ chỉ bạn cách xử lý dạng double bar chart này sao cho dễ nhìn ý và không bị nhầm số nha.

1. Hiểu đề bài

Biểu đồ gồm 2 phần:

Biểu đồ 1:

tỷ lệ phim được phát hành theo 4 thể loại:

  • Drama
  • Comedy
  • Fantasy
  • Romance

Biểu đồ 2:

tỷ lệ doanh số bán vé điện ảnh của cùng 4 thể loại đó.

Dữ liệu được so sánh giữa:

  • 1996
  • 2000

TID nhắc bạn:

Vì có 2 biểu đồ nên đừng viết tách rời hoàn toàn nha.

Hãy cố liên kết:

“thể loại nào phát hành nhiều” ↔ “thể loại nào bán vé tốt”.

2. Cách viết Introduction

Paraphrase đơn giản:

The two bar charts compare the percentages of films released and cinema ticket sales for four movie genres in 1996 and 2000\.

Là đủ nha.

3. Cách viết Overview

TID gợi ý overview như này:

Drama and comedy accounted for the largest proportions of films released in both years.

Comedy recorded the highest percentage of ticket sales, while romance remained the least popular category overall.

Most genres saw increases in both film releases and ticket sales between 1996 and 2000\.

TID lưu ý:

Overview chỉ cần nói:

  • cái lớn nhất
  • cái nhỏ nhất
  • xu hướng chung

Không cần nhét số nha.

4. Cách chia Body

BODY 1 – Percentage of films released

Drama:

  • 1996: khoảng 27%
  • 2000: 35%

→ cao nhất cả 2 năm

Comedy:

  • tăng từ 20% lên 25%

Fantasy:

  • tăng nhẹ từ khoảng 12% lên 16%

Romance:

  • giữ nguyên khoảng 6%

TID gợi ý:

Body này nên đi từ cao xuống thấp để bài logic hơn nha.

BODY 2 – Percentage of cinema ticket sales

Comedy:

  • cao nhất
  • tăng từ 20% lên khoảng 23%

Drama:

  • tăng nhẹ từ khoảng 16% lên 17%

Fantasy:

  • tăng đáng kể từ khoảng 3% lên 7%

Romance:

  • giảm từ khoảng 5% xuống 3%

→ thấp nhất năm 2000

TID lưu ý:

Fantasy là thể loại tăng mạnh nhất về ticket sales nha, dễ lấy làm highlight.

5. Gợi ý paraphrase

TID gợi ý vài cách diễn đạt:

accounted for / represented

rose from … to …

saw an increase

experienced significant growth

remained stable

declined slightly

Ví dụ:

Comedy accounted for the highest proportion of cinema ticket sales in both years.

The percentage of fantasy ticket sales increased considerably between 1996 and 2000\.

Romance films remained unchanged in terms of releases, while their ticket sales fell slightly nha.

The two bar charts compare the percentages of films released and cinema ticket sales for four movie genres, namely drama, comedy, fantasy and romance, in 1996 and 2000\.

Overall, drama and comedy accounted for the largest proportions of films released in both years. Comedy generated the highest percentage of cinema ticket sales, while romance remained the least popular genre overall. In general, most categories experienced growth between 1996 and 2000\.

In terms of film releases, drama was the most common genre, increasing from approximately 27% in 1996 to 35% in 2000\. Comedy also saw a noticeable rise, climbing from 20% to 25%. Similarly, the proportion of fantasy films released grew moderately from around 12% to 16%. By contrast, romance remained unchanged at roughly 6% over the period.

Regarding cinema ticket sales, comedy recorded the highest figures, rising from 20% in 1996 to about 23% in 2000\. Drama also experienced a slight increase, from around 16% to 17%. Fantasy, however, showed the most significant growth in ticket sales, more than doubling from approximately 3% to 7%. In contrast, romance ticket sales declined slightly from 5% to around 3%, making it the least successful genre in 2000\.

UNITS/AXES: Percentage (%); 1996, 2000
SERIES/CATEGORIES: Drama, Comedy, Fantasy, Romance
DATA:
Percentage of films released - 1996: Drama 27%, Comedy 20%, Fantasy 12%, Romance 6%
Percentage of films released - 2000: Drama 35%, Comedy 25%, Fantasy 16%, Romance 6%
Percentage of cinema ticket sales - 1996: Drama 16%, Comedy 20%, Fantasy 3%, Romance 5%
Percentage of cinema ticket sales - 2000: Drama 17%, Comedy 23%, Fantasy 7%, Romance 3%
KEY FEATURES:
* In 1996, Drama films were released the most, while Fantasy films had the lowest ticket sales.
* In 2000, Drama films were released the most, and Romance films had the lowest ticket sales.
* The percentage of films released increased for Drama, Comedy, and Fantasy from 1996 to 2000, while Romance remained stable.
* The percentage of cinema ticket sales increased for Drama, Comedy, and Fantasy from 1996 to 2000, but decreased for Romance.
* Comedy films consistently had the highest percentage of cinema ticket sales in both years.
* Romance films had a higher percentage of films released than ticket sales in both years.

IELTS Writing Task 1 – Internet use by age group

TID sẽ chỉ bạn cách xử lý dạng bar chart so sánh 2 nhóm tuổi across countries sao cho rõ ràng và dễ viết nha.

1. Hiểu đề bài

Biểu đồ so sánh tỷ lệ sử dụng Internet của 2 nhóm tuổi:

  • 55–64
  • 25–34

ở 6 quốc gia:

Germany, USA, Russia, South Korea, Brazil, China

TID nhắc bạn:

Dạng này cần:

  • so sánh giữa 2 nhóm tuổi
  • so sánh giữa các quốc gia
  • tìm pattern chung

2. Cách viết Introduction

Paraphrase đề bài, giữ đủ:

  • tỷ lệ (%)
  • 2 nhóm tuổi
  • các quốc gia

Viết gọn là được nha.

3. Cách viết Overview

TID gợi ý bạn các ý chính:

  • Nhóm 25–34 luôn có tỷ lệ cao hơn nhóm 55–64 ở hầu hết các quốc gia
  • South Korea và Germany có tỷ lệ cao nhất ở nhóm trẻ
  • China và Brazil có mức thấp nhất ở cả hai nhóm

Bạn cũng có thể thêm:

Khoảng cách giữa hai nhóm tuổi đặc biệt lớn ở South Korea

4. Cách chia Body

BODY 1 – Nhóm cao (Germany, USA, South Korea)
  • Germany:

\~85% (55–64) vs \~95% (25–34)

  • USA:

\~90% vs \~82%

(đây là nước hiếm hoi nhóm lớn tuổi cao hơn nha)

  • South Korea:

\~40% vs \~98%

(chênh lệch rất lớn)

TID gợi ý:

Bạn nên highlight South Korea vì gap rất rõ nha.

BODY 2 – Nhóm còn lại (Russia, Brazil, China)
  • Russia:

\~70% vs \~85%

  • Brazil:

\~25% vs \~55%

  • China:

\~15% vs \~22%

TID lưu ý:

Các nước này đều có mức thấp hơn và vẫn giữ pattern “trẻ cao hơn già” nha.

5. Gợi ý paraphrase

TID gợi ý bạn một số cách diễn đạt:

  • age group
  • proportion / percentage
  • internet users
  • higher than / lower than
  • gap / difference

Ví dụ:

Younger adults generally had higher rates of Internet use than older people across most countries nha.

The largest gap was observed in South Korea, where usage among younger people was significantly higher.

The bar chart compares the percentages of people in two age groups, 25–34 and 55–64, across six countries.

Overall, younger adults recorded higher proportions than older people in most countries, with the largest gap observed in South Korea. The USA is the only country where the older group slightly exceeded the younger group.

Germany and the USA showed the highest figures overall. In Germany, about 90 percent of those aged 25–34 were represented, compared to roughly 85 percent among 55–64 year olds. A similar pattern is seen in Russia, where the younger group stood at around 85 percent, exceeding the older group at approximately 70 percent. In contrast, the USA showed the reverse trend, with about 90 percent for older people compared to around 82 percent for younger adults.

The most pronounced difference appears in South Korea, where nearly 100 percent of the younger group was recorded, while the figure for the older group was only about 40 percent. Brazil and China had considerably lower levels overall, although the same pattern persisted, with younger people outnumbering older individuals, at roughly 55 versus 25 percent in Brazil and around 22 versus 15 percent in China.

title: Luyện đề IELTS Writing Task 1: Global market share of three computer operating systems - Pie Chart

logical_frame.name: Introduction
logical_frame.value: The pie charts illustrate the global market share of three computer operating systems and other systems from 2012 to 2015.

logical_frame.name: Overview
logical_frame.value: Overall, OS 1 experienced substantial growth throughout the period while Others showed a dramatic decline. By the end of the period, OS 1 had become the dominant operating system, capturing more than half of the market.

logical_frame.name: Body 1
logical_frame.value: Looking at the most dramatically changing categories, in 2012, Others held the largest market share at 48%, which was more than double that of OS 1 at 20%. However, OS 1 underwent remarkable expansion over the four-year period, surging to 38% in 2013, then to 47% in 2014, before reaching its peak of 52% in 2015. In contrast, Others experienced a precipitous decline, plummeting from nearly half of the market to 35% in 2013, then continuing its downward trajectory to 23% in 2014 and finally reaching a mere 15% by 2015.

logical_frame.name: Body 2
logical_frame.value: Regarding the more stable operating systems, OS 2 maintained a relatively consistent market share throughout the period, starting at 17% in 2012 and remaining at this level in 2013, before showing a marginal increase to 18% in both 2014 and 2015. Similarly, OS 3 demonstrated limited variation, beginning at 15% in 2012, dropping to its lowest point of 10% in 2013, then recovering slightly to 12% in 2014 before returning to 15% in the final year.

title: [YouPass Collect] - Overseas student residence patterns in Australia: 1982-2000

logical_frame.name: Introduction
logical_frame.value: The line graph illustrates the number of international students from four Asian countries who came to Australia for educational purposes between 1982 and 2000.

logical_frame.name: Overview
logical_frame.value: Overall, all four countries experienced an upward trend in student numbers throughout the given period, despite some fluctuations. Additionally, Malaysia started with the highest figure, but was eventually surpassed by Indonesia, which recorded the highest number by 2000.

logical_frame.name: Body 1
logical_frame.value: Looking at countries with sharper increases and subsequent declines, Indonesia began at zero in 1982 and rose gradually to 10,000 students by 1994. From there, the figure surged dramatically to peak at roughly 26,000 in 1998, before falling back to around 23,000 by 2000. Similarly, Hong Kong started later, with around 5,000 students in 1988, then climbed steadily to approximately 19,000 in 1997. However, this was followed by a decline to 14,000 in 1999, though the number recovered slightly to 18,000 in the final year.

logical_frame.name: Body 2
logical_frame.value: Regarding countries with more consistent growth patterns, Singapore started from zero while Malaysia recorded the highest initial figure of close to 5,000 in 1982. Singapore experienced steady growth throughout, multiplying nearly twentyfold to reach just under 20,000 by 2000, thereby overtaking Malaysia as the second most popular destination. Meanwhile, Malaysia more than tripled to peak at approximately 17,500 in 1997, then declined to around 15,000 in 1999, before recovering to roughly 17,000 in the final year, remaining in third place.

title: [11/8/2024] Car ownership in the UK

logical_frame.name: Introduction
logical_frame.value: The given line graph illustrates the proportions of the population owning one, two, three cars, and of those not owning one in Great Britain from 1975 to 2005.

logical_frame.name: Overview
logical_frame.value: Overall, possession of automobiles in the UK increased over the thirty-year period, and having one car remained the most popular throughout the years.

logical_frame.name: Body 1
logical_frame.value: At the start of the period, similar proportions of people had one car and no cars, with figures of 45% and 43%, respectively. Thereafter, both options declined in popularity in the first decade. Over the next twenty years, the percentage of single-car ownership followed an upward trend, finally ending up at 45% in 2005. After falling from 43% in 1975 to 25% in 1985, the proportion of non-car owners continued to decline more steadily, and at the end of the period, 22% of individuals did not own a car.

logical_frame.name: Body 2
logical_frame.value: Regarding households with multiple cars, only about 6% owned two cars in 1975, while the figure for three-car ownership was negligible at roughly 2%. Both categories showed gradual increases over the next three decades, with two-car households rising to about 18% and three-car families reaching nearly 10% by 2005.

title: [7/1/2024] Single student room Vs. Twin student room

logical_frame.name: Introduction
logical_frame.value: The floor plans illustrate the differences between two student rooms, designed for one and two occupants, at an Australian university.

logical_frame.name: Overview
logical_frame.value: Overall, the dual occupancy room is more spacious, with additional furnishings, and its rental cost is correspondingly higher compared to the single one.

logical_frame.name: Body 1 + Body 2
logical_frame.value:
In terms of size, both units share the same length of 6 meters. However, the two-person room has been designed with a greater width (4 meters) compared to the one-person room (2.5 meters), resulting in a higher weekly rental cost ($350 vs $200).
 
As the visitor enters the room, the two rooms display similar features on the left, namely a bathroom and a bookshelf. Beyond that, both have a study desk facing the wall and a bed by the back wall. However, the larger room is furnished with a circular table with two chairs outside the bathroom.

logical_frame.name: Body 3
logical_frame.value: Moving to the right-hand side of the entrance, both feature a kitchen that comes with a sink, a stove, and a microwave. However, the kitchen in the two-occupant room is in the corner opposite the bathroom, providing more space for cooking, while the single room's kitchen is located by the right-hand wall, offering a more confined cooking space when the door is open. Moreover, the space on the right-hand side of the twin room contains an additional study desk beside the TV, and a second bed, separated from the first one by two cupboards, while the single room is furnished with only a TV on this side, offering more usable space.

title: [14/10/2025] Nelson city from 2000 to now

logical_frame.name: Introduction
logical_frame.value: The maps illustrate the changes that have taken place in Nelson city centre between the year 2000 and the present day.

logical_frame.name: Overview
logical_frame.value: Overall, the area has undergone extensive redevelopment, with the addition of numerous commercial, residential, and recreational facilities. While certain landmarks such as the university and port have remained in their original locations, the city has made many significant improvements to its transportation infrastructure.

logical_frame.name: Body 1
logical_frame.value: Beginning with the northern section and transportation changes, the train station has been relocated from its original position in the west to a more central location. In the northwestern area, a hall of residence has been constructed on the west side of the university, which itself remains unchanged. To the northeast, the trees that once stood have been removed to make way for a new shopping centre. Additionally, a pedestrian crossing has been established, connecting the university to the city centre area.

logical_frame.name: Body 2
logical_frame.value: Turning to the city centre and southern areas, the open space previously labeled "City Centre" has been developed into a bike rental scheme. In the southwestern section, the old market has been demolished, and in its place, a new shop and a new covered market have been built on the west side and east side of the the bike rental area respectively. The road at the bottom of the map, which once accommodated vehicular traffic, has been converted into a pedestrian-only zone. Along this pedestrianized area, new establishments have emerged: a restaurant has opened to the southwest near the port, and bars and clubs have been established to the southeast. Finally, the port itself continues to operate in its original southern location.

title: [YouPass Collect] - Employment sector shifts across three countries

logical_frame.name: Introduction
logical_frame.value: The bar charts illustrate the percentages of the workforce employed in three economic sectors - agriculture, industry, and services - across three countries in 1980 and 2020.

logical_frame.name: Overview
logical_frame.value: Overall, employment in the services sector increased in all three countries over the 40-year period, while agricultural employment declined. In contrast, industrial employment showed mixed trends, decreasing in Countries A and C but rising substantially in Country B. title: [YouPass Collect] - Olive Oil Production Process

logical_frame.name: Introduction
logical_frame.value: The diagram illustrates the procedure for producing olive oil from harvested olives.

logical_frame.name: Overview
logical_frame.value: Overall, the process comprises several main stages: initial fruit collection and cleaning, mechanical oil extraction and final separation and storage of the products.

logical_frame.name: Body 1
logical_frame.value: Looking at the initial stages, olives are picked from the trees and deposited into collection vats where they are subjected to leaf removal and washing. Next, the cleaned fruit is transferred to an olive mill and crushed to form an olive paste. This paste then undergoes malaxation at temperatures below 27°C, a gentle mixing step that helps small oil droplets coalesce. After malaxation, the paste is directed into a centrifugal separator (centrifuge), where the bulk of the oil is mechanically extracted and separated from the solid material.

logical_frame.name: Body 2
logical_frame.value: From this stage onwards, the extracted liquid stream is subsequently treated to yield consumable oil and waste streams. Virgin oil is first transferred to a decanter for clarification, allowing solids and water to settle out. Any remaining liquid is passed through a separation stage in which residual wastewater is removed and either treated or discharged as effluent, while the purified oil is collected. The solid residue, or pomace, is removed from the centrifuge and transported for further refining or processing at specialist facilities. Finally, the clarified oil is deposited into a storage tank, ready for bottling or distribution.

title: [06/01/2024] - Recycling paper

logical_frame.name: Introduction
logical_frame.value: The diagram illustrates the process by which used paper is transformed into recycled paper through a series of four main stages.

logical_frame.name: Overview
logical_frame.value: Overall, the paper recycling process involves four distinct phases: making pulp, filtering, cleaning, and producing the final recycled paper. The entire procedure transforms waste paper into a reusable product through mechanical and chemical treatment methods.

logical_frame.name: Body 1
logical_frame.value: The process begins with used paper being placed on a conveyor belt and transported to the pulp-making stage. During this initial phase, the used paper is mixed with water and chemicals in a large container to create unfiltered pulp. Subsequently, this unfiltered pulp undergoes a filtering process, where it passes through a filtering system that removes larger impurities and debris, resulting in filtered pulp.

logical_frame.name: Body 2
logical_frame.value: Following filtration, the cleaned pulp enters the cleaning stage, where ink and other contaminants are removed. This is accomplished through the use of an air pump system, combined with water and soap, which effectively eliminates ink particles to produce clean pulp. In the final stage, the clean pulp is processed through heated rollers with additional water to create the finished recycled paper, which can then be reused for various purposes.

title: [20/4/2023] The recycling process of aluminium cans
description: The diagram below shows the recycling process of aluminium cans. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.

logical_frame.name: Introduction
logical_frame.value: The diagram illustrates the complete cycle of aluminium can recycling process in the UK, from collection to reuse.

logical_frame.name: Overview
logical_frame.value: Overall, this circular process consists of seven main stages with various mechanical and thermal procedures, beginning with the collection of used aluminium cans and ending with reusing.

logical_frame.name: Body 1
logical_frame.value: At the start, people dispose of used cans in designated aluminium recycling bins, which are then collected by recycling trucks. Following this, the cans undergo several preparatory steps including cleaning, sorting, shredding, and compressing. Thereafter, the processed material is then subjected to heating and melting, which transforms the solid aluminium into a liquid state.

logical_frame.name: Body 2
logical_frame.value: In the subsequent stage of the process, the melted aluminium is rolled into sheets measuring between 2.5mm and 6mm in thickness. These sheets then enter the recycling phase where they are formed into new cans. Finally, the cycle completes at the reusing stage, where 74% of aluminium cans are recycled to be distributed for consumer use.

logical_frame.name: Body 2

However, by 2010, this area had been dramatically transformed with the construction of a hydroelectric dam and the creation of a large lake. Multiple electricity transmission towers were installed across the region, and the irrigated farmland gave way to a new hotel. Despite these significant changes, the existing villages on this side of the river were also maintained.

title: [17/8/2024] The production of three forest industry products

logical_frame.value: The line graph illustrates the production volume of three forest industry products, namely timber, pulp, and paper, measured in million tonnes, in a European country between 1980 and 1996.

logical_frame.name: Overview
logical_frame.value: Overall, despite some fluctuations, all three products showed an upward trend in production over the twenty-year period. In addition, paper manufacturing experienced the most significant growth, ending the period as the highest-volume product.

logical_frame.name: Body 1
logical_frame.value: Looking at pulp production first, it started at approximately 4.5 million tonnes in 1980 and rose steadily to reach its peak of about 9.5 million tonnes in 1984. However, after this point, the figures began to decline gradually, falling to about 7.5 million tonnes by the end of the period, despite some minor fluctuations between 1990 and 1996.

logical_frame.name: Body 2
logical_frame.value: Regarding the other two products, in 1980, timber production began at a higher level of approximately 5.5 million tonnes, while paper output started at the lowest point among all three products, at around 3.8 million tonnes. Paper production then showed the most dramatic increase, rising consistently throughout the period to reach 12 million tonnes in 1996, making it the most-produced item. A similar but less pronounced upward trend was seen in timber output, though it first experienced a sharp drop to about 3 million tonnes in 1982, before recovering and growing steadily to end the period at approximately 9.5 million tonnes.

title: [7/1/2023] Reasons for university choice
description: The pie chart below shows the main reasons why students chose to study at a particular UK university in 1997 and 2007. Summarize the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.

logical_frame.name: Introduction
logical_frame.value: The pie charts compare five major factors that influenced students' decisions when choosing a UK university in 1997 and 2007.

logical_frame.name: Overview
logical_frame.value: Overall, while some reasons such as proximity to parental home became more important over the decade, others like sports and social activities declined significantly in relevance. Throughout both years, suitable degree courses remained the most commonly cited factor.

logical_frame.name: Body 1
logical_frame.value: Starting with the reasons that grew in importance, suitable degree courses was the dominant factor in both years, accounting for 35% of responses in 1997 before rising slightly to 37% a decade later. Meanwhile, proximity to parental home saw the most dramatic increase, more than doubling from 10% to 22% over the period. Quality of teaching also experienced a modest rise, climbing from 15% to 18%, making it the third most popular reason by 2007.

logical_frame.name: Body 2
logical_frame.value: As for the declining factors, the proportion of students who chose universities based on good sports and social activities fell sharply from 19% in 1997 to just 6% in 2007, representing the most significant decrease among all categories. Similarly, quality of resource, which was the second most important factor in 1997 at 21%, dropped to 17% over the same period, becoming less influential than proximity to home.

title: [13/10/2022] The production of perfume
description: The diagram below shows how oil is extracted in the production of perfume. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features and make comparisons where relevant.

logical_frame.name: Introduction
logical_frame.value: The diagram illustrates the process of extracting essential oils from aromatic plants to produce perfume through a distillation process.

logical_frame.name: Overview
logical_frame.value: The process consists of four stages, beginning with heating water to generate steam and ending with the separation of two final products: essential oil and aromatic water (hydrolat).

logical_frame.name: Body 1
logical_frame.value: The process starts when fire is applied to heat water in a container, which then generates steam. This steam passes through a chamber filled with aromatic plants, where it carries aromatic compounds from the plants along with it. At this stage, it forms a mixture of steam and oil vapor that flows into the condenser.

logical_frame.name: Body 2
logical_frame.value: In the latter stages, the aromatic steam vapor moves through a condensation chamber where cold water is pumped in to cool the vapor, while hot water exits as part of the cooling process. The condensed liquid, which is a mixture of water and essential oil, flows into a separation vessel. This specialized separator uses a distinctive Y-shaped design to divide the mixture, where the essential oil is extracted through one outlet, while the hydrolat (aromatic water) is collected through another as the final product.

title: [17/10/2023] Process for making soft cheese
description: The diagram below shows how soft cheese is made. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.

logical_frame.name: Introduction
logical_frame.value: The diagram illustrates the process of manufacturing soft cheese from milk and water.

logical_frame.name: Overview
logical_frame.value: The process undergoes five stages, beginning with the initial mixing of water and milk, and concluding with the cooling of the final product at a specific temperature.

logical_frame.name: Body 1
logical_frame.value: The process begins when water and milk are combined in a mixing chamber, where a mixture is formed. This mixture then enters the first cooling process, where it is maintained at 5 degrees Celsius for two hours. Following this, the mixture moves to the fermentation phase, where salt is added, and the mixture is heated to 37 degrees Celsius for a period of six hours.

logical_frame.name: Body 2
logical_frame.value: In the latter stages of production, the mixture is heated to 100 degrees Celsius during an evaporation process that lasts eight hours, producing steam as a by-product. Finally, in the final cooling stage, the soft cheese is cooled to 5 degrees Celsius for eight hours, during which waste water is removed through a filtration system, resulting in the finished soft cheese product.

title: [08/07/2023] The process of making cheese
description: The diagram below shows the process of making cheese. Summarize the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.

logical_frame.name: Introduction
logical_frame.value: The diagram illustrates the manufacturing process of cheese.

logical_frame.name: Overview
logical_frame.value: The process involves nine distinct stages, beginning with the draining of whey from curds and culminating in the production of ripened cheese.

logical_frame.name: Body 1
logical_frame.value: Initially, whey is drained from curds in a large container. Following this, the curds are broken down through a milling process into smaller pieces. Salt is then sprinkled over the milled curds as they move along a conveyor belt. At this stage, some of the mixture is collected to produce fresh cheese (cottage and cream cheese). The remaining seasoned mixture is then poured into molds to give the cheese its initial shape.

logical_frame.name: Body 2
logical_frame.value: In the subsequent stages, the cheese-filled molds are compressed using a pressing mechanism, during which additional whey is extracted. The pressed cheese pieces are then transferred to special shelves where they are left to mature for a period of time. The end result of this process is fully ripened cheese, which appears as rounded blocks ready for consumption.

title: [C18T4] Average monthly change in prices of three metals

logical_frame.name: Overview

The most dramatic variations were seen in nickel prices, which peaked early in the year before sharply declining by mid-year.

logical_frame.name: Body 1
logical_frame.value: Looking at nickel specifically, this metal recorded the highest monthly price increase of approximately 6% in January, followed by a steep decline to approximately 4% in February. After maintaining relatively stable price changes around 1% from March to May, nickel saw its sharpest price drop to -3% in June, before gradually recovering to end the year at roughly 1% above the previous month's price.

logical_frame.name: Body 2
logical_frame.value: Regarding the other two metals, both zinc and copper began 2014 with modest price increases of about 1% and 2% respectively. Zinc then rose to nearly 3% in February before declining to -1% in June and leveled off for the next four months. Meanwhile, copper showed less dramatic changes, fluctuating between 0% and 1% for most of the year. By December, both metals recorded similar price increases of approximately 2%.

title: [C16T2] The production of sugar from sugar cane
description: The diagram shows the manufacturing process for making sugar from sugar cane. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.

logical_frame.name: Introduction
logical_frame.value: The diagram illustrates the steps involved in manufacturing sugar from sugar cane plants.

logical_frame.name: Overview
logical_frame.value: The process consists of seven main stages which transform raw sugar cane into refined sugar crystals, beginning with growing sugar cane and ending with drying and cooling the final product.

logical_frame.name: Body 1
logical_frame.value: The process starts when sugar cane is grown over a period of 12 to 18 months. Once mature, the canes are harvested using both mechanical equipment and manual labor. The harvested canes then undergo crushing, during which juice is extracted using large rollers.

logical_frame.name: Body 2
logical_frame.value: The remaining steps focus on refining the juice into pure sugar. First, the juice passes through a limestone filter for purification, after which it enters an evaporator where heat is applied to turn it into syrup. This syrup is then processed in a centrifuge to separate sugar crystals from the remaining liquid. Finally, these crystals undergo drying and cooling to produce the finished sugar product.
